body_en: Judge extends deadline for Trump’s deposition in $10bn BBC lawsuit | Donald Trump
President, who had agreed to sit for deposition in October but backed out, must now appear by 22 January
Donald Trump has been granted a temporary delay before he must give a witness statement in his $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC.

In late October, Enjoliqué Lett, a federal magistrate judge, gave Trump a firm 11 December deadline to sit for a deposition by lawyers representing the BBC in his lawsuit against the British broadcaster. If he failed to do so by that date, he could be subject to penalties up to dismissal of the case, the judge warned.

But on Tuesday, the president got something of a reprieve when Jeffrey Kuntz, a federal district court judge, approved a joint motion by the parties and extended the deadline for Trump’s deposition until 22 January. The judge also pushed back the deadline for discovery in the case from 18 December to 29 January.
Trump nominates Chris LaNeve as army chief after Hegseth fired predecessor

Trump had originally agreed to sit for a deposition on 16 October, but his team backed out, citing “matters of national importance”. That led the BBC to file a motion to compel Trump to sit for a deposition in a timely fashion.

According to the joint motion filed on Monday, the BBC has agreed to the Trump team’s proposal for the president to sit for a deposition between 11 January and 22 January after his representatives said he was unavailable to do so this year “due to his schedule and the nature of his profession”. As that timeline nears, the parties will meet to select a date and identify a secure location for the deposition.
“It is Trump’s case, so he should expect to be deposed,” Kuntz wrote in his order. “It appears he acknowledges that reality.”
The judge ordered the parties to schedule Trump’s deposition by Friday at noon. Kuntz scheduled a trial date for the case for 3 May 2027 in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

So far, Trump’s lawyers have deposed seven defendant witnesses. As part of the agreement between Trump and the BBC, the president’s lawyers will not depose Samir Shah, the BBC chair, or a former BBC director-general – nor any current or former BBC employee – until the president sits for questioning.
While Trump’s seven-hour-long deposition will be videotaped, it will only be available to attorneys for the parties.

In addition to Trump, the BBC might also be able to depose his daughter, Ivanka Trump, his son, Donald Trump Jr, and his son-in-law Jared Kushner. “Defendant is currently conferring with President Trump and these non-parties regarding the subpoenas directed to them, given that these non-parties may be objecting to, or moving to quash, those subpoenas,” the parties wrote in their joint motion.

Last week, Kuntz, a Trump appointee, refused the BBC’s request to dismiss the case , though he threw out the president’s contention that the broadcaster violated Florida’s Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act.

The lawsuit stems from a Panorama documentary aired by the BBC that spliced together two comments made nearly an hour apart by Trump during a rally on 6 January 2021, before the US Capitol riot. The BBC has acknowledged that this specific edit was misleading, but Trump has gone on to claim, falsely, that the BBC did not just edit his speech but used AI to insert words into his speech.
“BBC tries to frame this editing as ordinary editing done to condense a 70-minute-long speech into 12 seconds,” the judge wrote in his ruling. “But the court is not persuaded.”
body_zh: 法官延长特朗普在价值 100 亿美元的 BBC 诉讼中作证的最后期限唐纳德·特朗普
总统曾同意在 10 月份出庭作证，但后来退出，现在必须在 1 月 22 日之前出庭
唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 在针对 BBC 提起的价值 100 亿美元的诽谤诉讼中，获得了暂时推迟提交证人证词的许可。
10 月底，联邦地方法官 Enjoliqué Lett 给了特朗普一个严格的截止日期，即 12 月 11 日，让代表 BBC 的律师在针对英国广播公司的诉讼中出庭作证。法官警告说，如果他未能在该日期之前这样做，他可能会受到处罚，直至案件被驳回。
但周二，联邦地区法院法官杰弗里·昆茨 (Jeffrey Kuntz) 批准了双方的联合动议，并将特朗普作证的最后期限延长至 1 月 22 日，总统得到了一定程度的缓刑。法官还将该案的证据披露截止日期从 12 月 18 日推迟至 1 月 29 日。
赫格斯解雇前任陆军参谋长后，特朗普提名克里斯·拉内夫担任陆军参谋长
特朗普原本同意在 10 月 16 日出庭作证，但他的团队以“事关国家重大”为由退出。这导致英国广播公司 (BBC) 提出动议，迫使特朗普及时出庭作证。
根据周一提交的联合动议，BBC 已同意特朗普团队的提议，即总统在 1 月 11 日至 1 月 22 日期间出庭作证，此前特朗普的代表表示，“由于他的日程安排和职业性质”，他今年无法这样做。随着该时间表的临近，双方将举行会议以选择日期并确定安全的取证地点。
“这是特朗普的情况，所以他应该预料到会被废黜，”昆茨在他的命令中写道。 “看来他承认这个现实。”
法官命令双方在周五中午之前安排特朗普的证词。 Kuntz 计划于 2027 年 5 月 3 日在佛罗里达州劳德代尔堡审理此案。
到目前为止，特朗普的律师已经罢免了七名被告证人。作为特朗普与 BBC 之间协议的一部分，在总统接受质询之前，总统的律师不会罢免 BBC 主席萨米尔·沙阿 (Samir Shah) 或前 BBC 总干事 — — 也不会罢免任何现任或前任 BBC 员工。
虽然特朗普长达七小时的证词将被录像，但只有当事人的律师才能看到。
除了特朗普之外，BBC 或许还可以废黜他的女儿伊万卡·特朗普、儿子小唐纳德·特朗普和女婿贾里德·库什纳。各方在联合动议中写道：“被告目前正在与特朗普总统和这些非当事人就向他们发出的传票进行协商，因为这些非当事人可能会反对或准备撤销这些传票。”
上周，特朗普任命的昆茨拒绝了 BBC 驳回此案的请求，不过他驳斥了总统关于该广播公司违反佛罗里达州《欺骗和不公平贸易行为法》的论点。
该诉讼源于 BBC 播出的一部全景纪录片，该纪录片将特朗普在 2021 年 1 月 6 日美国国会大厦骚乱之前的一次集会上发表的两段相隔近一个小时的言论拼接在一起。 BBC 承认这种特定的编辑具有误导性，但特朗普继续错误地声称，BBC 不仅编辑了他的演讲，还使用人工智能在他的演讲中插入了单词。
法官在裁决中写道：“BBC 试图将这次剪辑视为普通剪辑，将 70 分钟长的演讲压缩为 12 秒。” “但法院并没有被说服。”

title_en: Trump brushes off NSA internal network outage: ‘it’s like that when you’re big and powerful’ – live
title_zh: 特朗普对美国国家安全局内部网络中断不予理睬：“当你又大又强的时候就会这样”——直播
summary: President’s words could be seen to run counter to NSA’s claim of ‘scheduled routine maintenance’ causing temporary issue Sign up for US Breaking News email Abdul El-Sayed , the Democratic-Senator elect from Michigan, said today that he would be happy to work w
summary_zh: 总统的话可能会被视为与美国国家安全局关于“定期例行维护”导致暂时问题的说法背道而驰
body_en: Donald Trump brushed off reports that the National Security Agency’s internal network is down in remarks to reporters in Manila today, saying “it’s fine.”
“It’s like when you’re big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said.
As we reported earlier, an NSA spokesperson told the Guardian the outage was the result of “scheduled routine maintenance.”
But after a series of high profile outages over the past week – affecting banks, air traffic control, United Airlines and Microsoft – some have begun to raise concerns.
“If this is all a coincidence, it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world,” Republican senator Josh Hawley told reporters today.
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普今天在马尼拉对记者发表讲话时，对有关国家安全局内部网络瘫痪的报道不予理睬，称“没事”。
“这就像当你又大又强大，而且你拥有所有的钱时。这样的事情发生了。没关系，”特朗普说。
正如我们之前报道的，美国国家安全局发言人告诉《卫报》，这次中断是“预定的例行维护”的结果。
但在过去一周发生一系列引人注目的停电事件之后——影响了银行、空中交通管制、联合航空和微软——一些人开始引起担忧。
“如果这一切都是巧合，那就像是世界历史上最伟大的巧合，”共和党参议员乔什·霍利今天对记者说。

body_en: Trump nominates Chris LaNeve as army chief after Hegseth fired predecessor | US military
LaNeve, who served as Hegseth’s senior military commander, nominated to permanently replace Gen Randy George

Donald Trump has nominated Gen Chris LaNeve to be the US army’s top officer, making permanent his interim service after the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth , unexpectedly fired his predecessor in April.
LaNeve had been serving as Hegseth’s senior military commander before his nomination for a fourth star and service as vice-chief of staff of the army in February.

“For 36 years, I’ve served in the U.S. Army, currently as the Vice Chief of Staff,” LaNeve said in a statement released by the Pentagon. “I’m deeply honored by the President’s trust and confidence for the nomination to serve as the Chief of Staff of the U.S. Army and if confirmed, I look forward to continuing to serve our Solders, their families and our nation.”

Two months later, Hegseth fired the army chief of staff, Gen Randy George. While the firing has never been explained, George had insisted on an official investigation into an unauthorized 28 March army helicopter flyover near the Tennessee home of musician Kid Rock, which Hegseth blocked.
LaNeve’s relatively short tenure as a four-star general has raised questions among Democrats and Republicans, according to reporting from the Wall Street Journal.

LaNeve, 59, graduated from the University of Arizona in 1990 and later earned master’s degrees from Central Michigan University and the US Army Command and General Staff College. He has served in a wide variety of command roles, including a rotation as the commander of the 82nd Airborne Division and the 8th Army in Korea.
body_zh: 赫格斯解雇前任后，特朗普提名克里斯·拉内夫担任陆军参谋长美军
担任赫格赛斯高级军事指挥官的拉内夫被提名永久接替兰迪·乔治将军
唐纳德·特朗普提名克里斯·拉内夫将军为美国陆军最高军官，在国防部长皮特·赫格斯四月份意外解雇了他的前任后，他的临时职务永久化。
拉内夫在二月份被提名为第四星并担任陆军副参谋长之前，一直担任赫格斯塞斯的高级军事指挥官。
拉内夫在五角大楼发布的一份声明中表示：“我在美国陆军服役了 36 年，目前担任副参谋长。” “总统对我任命为美国陆军参谋长的信任和信心让我深感荣幸，如果得到确认，我期待继续为我们的士兵、他们的家人和我们的国家服务。”
两个月后，赫格斯解雇了陆军参谋长兰迪·乔治将军。虽然枪击事件从未得到解释，但乔治坚持要求对 3 月 28 日未经授权的军用直升机飞越音乐家基德·洛克 (Kid Rock) 田纳西州家附近的一次未经授权的飞行进行正式调查，但赫格斯阻止了这一事件。
据《华尔街日报》报道，拉内夫作为四星将军的任期相对较短，引起了民主党和共和党的质疑。
拉内夫现年 59 岁，1990 年毕业于亚利桑那大学，后获得中央密歇根大学和美国陆军指挥与参谋学院硕士学位。他曾担任过多种指挥职务，包括轮流担任驻韩第 82 空降师和第 8 集团军的指挥官。

title_en: Cornyn links Nvidia scandal to perception of Trump admin corruption
title_zh: 科宁将英伟达丑闻与特朗普政府腐败的看法联系起来
summary: The outgoing Texas Republican senator said “the buck stops with [Trump]” when pressed on whether the White House plays a role in the appearance of corruption and self-dealing.
summary_zh: 当被问及白宫是否在特朗普的出现中发挥作用时，这位即将离任的德克萨斯州共和党参议员表示，“责任归特朗普所有”。
body_en: Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn sees the Nvidia scandal and questions about the Trump administration’s alleged lax chip export control rules as part of a broader perception of corruption, which he said contributed to the Republican drubbing in the midterms.

“Let’s talk about Nvidia and export controls,” the Texas Republican said when asked to name examples of corruption he sees at the federal level during an onstage interview at the Atlantic Summit on Tuesday.

He then pointed to media reports that advanced Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China through the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and that the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, resisted efforts by other Cabinet agencies to crack down on Megaspeed.

“I just think there’s a lot of things that will be investigated, and we’ll learn more about, basically, this perception that there was self-dealing going on that I think caused a lot of unease by the American people,” Cornyn said.

He said President Donald Trump is at the center of the perceived corruption — “the buck stops with him” — and that many congressional Republicans, fearing the White House’s retribution, have chosen not to cross the president publicly.

Cornyn’s remarks come as fallout from the Nvidia turmoil that led to CEO Jensen Huang’s ouster continues to roil Washington. The Trump administration is scrambling to further restrict China’s access to the most advanced American chips as pressure mounts from Capitol Hill, which is also set to hear testimony from Huang and Lutnick in the coming weeks.

The four-term senator, who lost his primary earlier this year to the Trump-endorsed Ken Paxton, did not mince words when asked about the cause of the blue wave that swept even statewide offices across his home state. “Well, President Trump said he was on the ballot.”

In a pair of statements, White House spokespeople blamed Democrats for refusing “to do anything to stop waste, fraud, and abuse in our government” and highlighted the Commerce Department’s interim final rule to “crack down on the smuggling of advanced U.S. SI chips, including through third countries and remote access by Chinese SI labs.”

“The Trump Administration will continue to take decisive action to protect America’s technological edge, strengthen our national security, and ensure the future of SI is built in America,” White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton said.
Cornyn in his remarks Tuesday also urged Washington to keep China as its top national security and foreign policy focus, as Trump is set to meet with China’s leader Xi Jinping later this week.

He warned about disruption to the semiconductor supply chain should China try to invade Taiwan, its island democracy neighbor that produces an overwhelming majority of the world’s most advanced chips.

“The idea that there could be another pandemic or military conflict or natural disaster that would disrupt that ought to worry everybody,” he said. “That’s one of my principal concerns is what China may or may not do in the Taiwan Straits.”
body_zh: 即将离任的参议员约翰·科宁 (John Cornyn) 将英伟达丑闻和有关特朗普政府所谓宽松的芯片出口管制规则的问题视为更广泛的腐败认知的一部分，他表示，这导致了共和党在中期选举中惨败。
“让我们来谈谈英伟达和出口管制，”这位得克萨斯州共和党人在周二大西洋峰会的台上采访中被问及他在联邦层面看到的腐败例子时说道。
随后，他指出媒体报道称，先进的英伟达芯片可能已通过新加坡公司 Megaspeed 转移到中国，而由部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 领导的商务部抵制了其他内阁机构打击 Megaspeed 的努力。
科宁说：“我只是认为有很多事情需要调查，我们基本上会更多地了解这种认为存在自我交易行为的看法，我认为这引起了美国人民的很多不安。”
他说，唐纳德·特朗普总统是腐败的中心——“责任归他所有”——许多国会共和党人担心白宫的报复，选择不公开反对总统。
科宁发表上述言论之际，英伟达公司的混乱导致首席执行官黄仁勋被罢免，其余波继续扰乱华盛顿。随着来自国会山的压力越来越大，特朗普政府正在争先恐后地进一步限制中国获得最先进的美国芯片，国会山也将在未来几周内听取黄仁勋和卢特尼克的证词。
这位四届参议员今年早些时候在初选中输给了特朗普支持的肯·帕克斯顿(Ken Paxton)，当被问及席卷他家乡甚至全州办公室的蓝色浪潮的原因时，他毫不拐弯抹角。 “嗯，特朗普总统说他参加了投票。”
在两份声明中，白宫发言人指责民主党拒绝“采取任何措施制止我国政府的浪费、欺诈和滥用行为”，并强调了商务部的临时最终规则，即“打击走私美国先进的 SI 芯片，包括通过第三国和中国 SI 实验室的远程访问。”
白宫发言人马修·米德尔顿表示：“特朗普政府将继续采取果断行动，保护美国的技术优势，加强我们的国家安全，并确保 SI 的未来建立在美国。”
科宁在周二的讲话中还敦促华盛顿继续将中国作为其国家安全和外交政策的最高焦点，因为特朗普将于本周晚些时候会见中国领导人习近平。
他警告说，如果中国试图入侵台湾，半导体供应链将受到破坏。台湾是台湾的岛国民主邻国，世界上绝大多数最先进的芯片都由台湾生产。
他说：“可能会出现另一场流行病、军事冲突或自然灾害，从而扰乱这一局面，这一想法应该让所有人感到担忧。” “我主要担心的问题之一是中国在台湾海峡可能会做什么或不会做什么。”

body_en: Jensen Huang to testify before Congress on ‘potential breach of national security’ | Jensen Huang
High-stakes hearing comes in wake of resignation from Nvidia after alleged affair with suspected Chinese spy

Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang will testify before several congressional committees on 1 December, setting the stage for a high-stakes hearing in the wake of his resignation following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, has also agreed to appear for a closed-door transcribed interview the following day, 2 December.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” Congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, who chair the committees, said in a press release. “The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous [People’s Republic of China] actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal.”
Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return to Nvidia as CEO

The three congressmen chair the foreign affairs committee, the select committee on the Chinese Communist party, and the intelligence committee of the House of Representatives, respectively. On 12 November, they had signed a letter warning Huang that he could face a subpoena if he did not agree to the closed-door meeting.
Nvidia chips are key to powering the artificial intelligence boom. The Trump administration has prohibited the selling of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China.
Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO after allegations of extramarital relationships with the suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees surfaced.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, had been Megaspeed International’s executive director. The Singapore-based cloud computing company has bought nearly $5bn in AI chips and advanced hardware. The company said Alice Huang stepped down in 2025.

Megaspeed ultimately facilitated about $12bn in chip sales, i n violation of US export controls. On Friday, Malaysia stated that they were investigating whether the company diverted advanced AI ships to other countries.

A recent joint Department of Commerce and Department of Justice letter, stated that the Department of Commerce , under its secretary, Howard Lutnick, first started an investigation in Megaspeed on 2024 for potential export control violations. The justice department, led by the attorney general, Todd Blanche, took over in 2025.

In his first remarks since his resignation, Jensen Huang said on Thursday he would be willing to return to Nvidia as CEO. Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley tech giants, along with 165,000 signatories to an open letter, have called for his reinstatement. Trump has also signaled his openness for the disgraced tech CEO’s return.
body_zh: 黄仁勋将就“潜在违反国家安全”问题在国会作证 |黄仁勋
英伟达因涉嫌与中国间谍嫌疑人有染而辞职，召开高风险听证会
英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋将于 12 月 1 日在多个国会委员会作证，为他因与一名涉嫌中国间谍有染而辞职后举行的高风险听证会奠定基础。
Nvidia 总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特 (Tim Teter) 也同意在第二天（12 月 2 日）接受闭门采访。

委员会主席、国会议员布莱恩·马斯特 (Brian Mast)、约翰·穆勒纳尔 (John Moolenaar) 和里克·克劳福德 (Rick Crawford) 在一份新闻稿中表示：“我们期待听取黄仁勋和蒂姆·泰特的意见，了解他们在可能违反我们国家安全的行为中所扮演的角色。” “美国人民需要了解黄先生和英伟达在允许危险的[中华人民共和国]行为者获取我们最先进的芯片方面所扮演的角色，以及潜在的中国情报资产在这起丑闻中所扮演的角色。”
黄仁勋表示，他将“很荣幸”重返 Nvidia 担任首席执行官
三名国会议员分别担任众议院外交事务委员会、中国共产党特别委员会和情报委员会主席。 11月12日，他们签署了一封信，警告黄如果不同意闭门会议，他可能会面临传票。
英伟达芯片是推动人工智能热潮的关键。特朗普政府已禁止向中国出售先进的人工智能芯片。
在与涉嫌中国间谍黄爱丽和两名英伟达员工发生婚外情的指控浮出水面后，黄仁勋辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。
Alice Huang，又名黄乐，曾任Megaspeed International 的执行董事。这家总部位于新加坡的云计算公司已购买近 50 亿美元的人工智能芯片和先进硬件。该公司表示，Alice Huang 将于 2025 年辞职。
Megaspeed 最终促进了约 120 亿美元的芯片销售，违反了美国的出口管制。周五，马来西亚表示，他们正在调查该公司是否将先进的人工智能船只转移到其他国家。
美国商务部和司法部最近的一封联合信函指出，商务部在其部长霍华德·卢特尼克 (Howard Lutnick) 的领导下，于 2024 年首次对 Megaspeed 展开调查，调查其可能违反出口管制规定。由总检察长托德·布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 领导的司法部于 2025 年接管。
周四，黄仁勋在辞职后的首次讲话中表示，他愿意重返英伟达担任首席执行官。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和其他硅谷科技巨头，以及一封公开信的 165,000 名签名者，呼吁让他复职。特朗普还表示，他对这位名誉扫地的科技公司首席执行官的回归持开放态度。

body_en: US officials ‘debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute’ plot to detonate a ‘dirty bomb’, report says

Donald Trump has claimed the US is “looking into” whether Iran is developing plans to detonate a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington, even as the White House said there were “no credible threats” at this time.
Trump said his administration takes the idea “very seriously”

After a CNN report , citing seven unnamed US officials, that new US intelligence suggested Iran was working on plans that would use a dirty bomb, which combines conventional explosives with radioactive material, or a chemical weapon against senior Trump administration officials.
The report noted, however, that US officials “continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute such a plot”.

The US president’s war on Iran is deeply unpopular among Americans. His Republican party was widely rejected by voters in the midterm elections, in which the GOP lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives.

Asked in the Philippines on Tuesday if there was reason to believe that such an Iranian attack was imminent, Trump said: “If there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before. I hope it’s not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to ​be crazy.”
Lauren Bis, a White House spokesperson, said in a statement: “We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland.”

CNN cited the unnamed officials as saying that Tehran’s planning was an effort by Iran to “give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack”, but the plans include specific locations and targets.
While the plans would signify that Iran is willing to escalate its tactics against the US, there is no evidence to suggest they will go ahead with them.

The US and Israel went to war with Iran starting in February, with early airstrikes killing Iranian officials, including the supreme leader, Ali Khamenei. Trump has repeatedly claimed the war will be over soon, but it has continued.

The US president has argued that US involvement in the war is necessary so that the country does not build nuclear weapons. Iran has blocked trade through the strait of Hormuz, creating rising fuel costs – and rattling the global economy.
body_zh: 报告称，美国官员“争论伊朗是否能够或将尝试执行”引爆“脏弹”的阴谋
唐纳德·特朗普声称美国正在“调查”伊朗是否正在制定在华盛顿引爆所谓“脏弹”的计划，尽管白宫表示目前“没有可信的威胁”。
特朗普表示，他的政府“非常认真地”对待这个想法
美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 援引七名未透露姓名的美国官员的报道称，美国的新情报表明，伊朗正在制定计划，使用脏弹（将常规炸药与放射性物质结合在一起）或化学武器来对付特朗普政府高级官员。
然而，报告指出，美国官员“继续争论伊朗是否能够或将试图执行这样的阴谋”。
美国总统对伊朗的战争在美国人中极不受欢迎。他领导的共和党在中期选举中遭到选民广泛拒绝，共和党失去了参众两院的控制权。
周二在菲律宾被问及是否有理由相信伊朗即将发动袭击时，特朗普表示：“如果有的话，他们将付出前所未有的代价。我希望不是，但我们非常认真地对待它，因为他们碰巧疯了。”
白宫发言人劳伦·比斯在一份声明中表示：“我们仍然保持警惕，监控任何和所有潜在威胁，但目前还没有对祖国构成可信的威胁。”
美国有线电视新闻网援引未透露姓名的官员的话说，德黑兰的计划是伊朗“为自己提供选择，而不是即将发生袭击的指标”的努力，但计划包括具体地点和目标。
虽然这些计划表明伊朗愿意升级针对美国的策略，但没有证据表明他们会继续实施。
美国和以色列从二月份开始与伊朗开战，早期的空袭导致伊朗官员死亡，其中包括最高领导人阿里·哈梅内伊。特朗普一再声称战争很快就会结束，但战争仍在继续。
美国总统辩称，美国有必要参与这场战争，这样美国就不会制造核武器。伊朗封锁了霍尔木兹海峡的贸易，导致燃料成本上升 — — 并扰乱了全球经济。

FAA Tech Upgrade Update, Trump Asia Agenda, Petition To Reinstate Huang At Nvidia

A technology issue with United Airlines delayed departing flights yesterday evening , just as air travel was returning to normal after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday. President Trump said yesterday that he hopes this incident will prompt Congress to allocate more funds to upgrade the outdated air traffic control system.

A person looks at a departures board showing delays and cancellations at LaGuardia airport on November 13, 2026 in the Queens borough of New York City. Adam Gray/Getty Images North America hide caption

🎧 Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the FAA will reevaluate future maintenance procedures, NPR's Joe Hernandez tells Up First . Mike McCormick, a former FAA senior executive and air traffic manager, told Hernandez that he thinks another nationwide ground stop is unlikely. McCormick says that in cases like this, the FAA sometimes imposes a maintenance moratorium , temporarily halting such work. The ground stop happened while L3Harris workers converted copper wires to a fiber optic system and installed a new router in El Dorado, Arkansas.

President Trump is in Manila today to meet with allies at the ASEAN summit. Tomorrow, he travels to Shenzhen, China, for a joint summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. It's the first time those three have had a joint summit. The meeting will happen on the sidelines of the APEC summit that Xi is hosting in Shenzhen.

🎧 When leaving the White House yesterday, Trump said they would discuss his "favorite subject": Ukraine, NPR's Deepa Shivaram says. The White House had previously announced that Ukraine would not be on the agenda for the trilateral meeting. Shivaram says that Europe and Ukraine are concerned about how Ukraine may be discussed at the meeting, and what might come out of it, because President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will not be at APEC and Trump has recently been more lenient toward Putin and Russia.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation has shaken Silicon Valley , prompting calls from some tech leaders for the board to reinstate him. Trump said he agreed with them. Meanwhile, the U.S. government introduced a rule to block remote access to advanced AI chips and servers, closing a loophole that could allow adversarial governments to access American AI technology through overseas data centers. Nvidia is the world's dominant producer of AI chips.

🎧 Many prominent AI and venture capital figures have recognized Huang as a visionary whose company played a significant role in the AI boom, NPR's Shannon Bond says. An online petition supporting his reinstatement has garnered more than 160,000 signatures , but Bond says some of them may not be real. Elon Musk says he signed it. Brad Gerstner from Altimeter Capital, a key Nvidia investor, has urged the board to thoroughly investigate and keep all options open. Bond says the interim CEO and CFO will address the public for the first time following today's earnings report.

Prosecutors are moving to retry Lindsay Clancy for the deaths of her three children. The new trial is set for March 29, 2027 . Although there was speculation about potentially reducing the charges to manslaughter or second-degree murder after her previous trial ended in a mistrial, no changes were made during Monday's court hearing. Judge William Sullivan, who presided over the first trial, will oversee the new proceedings. He denied Clancy's defense team's request to dismiss the charges based on double jeopardy. Clancy's defense argues that she shouldn't be held criminally responsible for killing her children because she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis.
Dressed in costumes for Halloween, students of Kids Campus SFCC play at the playground in Santa Fe, New Mexico. Nina Alexandria Riggio for NPR hide caption

One year ago, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to all families regardless of income, as long as adults are working, seeking work, in school, or unable to work. Many parents have found this initiative life-changing, but capacity was limited. Only 50% of the some 67,000 children ages 5 and under are enrolled in the universal childcare program. Some of the remaining families participate in other programs, such as PreK and Head Start. New Mexico officials say the program must expand to meet demand. The issues observed in New Mexico are mirrored across the nation, prompting policymakers and childcare advocates to closely monitor the state's initiative .
👶 Almost half of U.S. children aged 5 and under live in licensed childcare deserts, where demand exceeds availability, according to the Center for American Progress, a left-leaning think tank.
👶 New Mexico's program has an operating budget of nearly $600 million, but some lawmakers are concerned it could be $50 million over budget this year.

👶 New Mexico state Sen. Steve Lanier tells NPR that the steep cost of the program is why he only supports universal childcare for some people, since someone earning around $450,000 or $600,000 might not need assistance. Lanier has previously sued to end the initiative, but the lawsuit was unsuccessful.

👶 Since the enactment of free, universal childcare in New Mexico, lower-income mothers have experienced significant gains. Their full-time employment has risen by 23%, according to a new paper from Arizona State University.

昨天晚上，美国联邦航空管理局下令在全国范围内停飞后，航空旅行正在恢复正常，联合航空公司的技术问题导致出发航班延误。特朗普总统昨天表示，他希望这一事件能够促使国会拨款更多资金来升级过时的空中交通管制系统。

🎧 NPR 的 Joe Hernandez 告诉 Up First，交通部长 Sean Duffy 表示，FAA 将重新评估未来的维护程序。美国联邦航空局前高级管理人员兼空中交通经理迈克·麦考密克告诉埃尔南德斯，他认为不太可能再在全国范围内进行地面停留。麦考密克说，在这种情况下，美国联邦航空局有时会暂停维护，暂时停止此类工作。地面停车发生在 L3Harris 工人将铜线转换为光纤系统并在阿肯色州埃尔多拉多安装新路由器时。

NPR 的迪帕·希瓦拉姆 (Deepa Shivaram) 表示，昨天离开白宫时，特朗普表示他们将讨论他“最喜欢的话题”：乌克兰。白宫此前曾宣布，乌克兰不会出现在三边会议议程上。希瓦拉姆表示，欧洲和乌克兰担心会议上如何讨论乌克兰问题以及会议可能产生什么结果，因为泽连斯基总统不会参加亚太经合组织，而特朗普最近对普京和俄罗斯更加宽容。
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的辞职震动了硅谷，促使一些科技领袖呼吁董事会恢复他的职位。特朗普表示他同意他们的观点。与此同时，美国政府出台了一项规则，阻止远程访问先进的人工智能芯片和服务器，堵住了敌对政府通过海外数据中心访问美国人工智能技术的漏洞。英伟达是全球领先的人工智能芯片生产商。

NPR 的香农·邦德 (Shannon Bond) 表示，许多著名的人工智能和风险投资人士都认为黄仁勋是一位有远见的人，他的公司在人工智能繁荣中发挥了重要作用。一份支持他复职的在线请愿书已获得超过 16 万个签名，但邦德表示其中一些可能不是真实的。埃隆·马斯克说他签了字。 Nvidia 的主要投资者 Altimeter Capital 的布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 敦促董事会彻底调查并保留所有选择。邦德表示，临时首席执行官和首席财务官将在今天的收益报告发布后首次向公众发表讲话。

检察官正着手对林赛·克兰西三个孩子的死亡案进行重审。新审判定于 2027 年 3 月 29 日进行。尽管在她之前的审判以误审结束后，有人猜测可能会将指控减少为过失杀人或二级谋杀，但周一的法庭听证会没有做出任何改变。主持第一次审判的威廉·沙利文法官将监督新的诉讼程序。他拒绝了克兰西辩护团队基于双重危险驳回指控的请求。克兰西的辩护律师认为，她不应该因杀害孩子而被追究刑事责任，因为她患有严重的产后精神病。
SFCC 儿童校园的学生身着万圣节服装，在新墨西哥州圣达菲的操场上玩耍。尼娜·亚历山大·里吉奥 (Nina Alexandria Riggio) 为 NPR 隐藏标题栏

一年前，新墨西哥州成为第一个向所有家庭提供免费托儿服务的州，无论其收入如何，只要成年人正在工作、寻找工作、在校或无法工作。许多家长发现这一举措改变了他们的生活，但能力有限。约 67,000 名 5 岁及以下儿童中，只有 50% 参加了全民托儿计划。剩下的一些家庭参加其他计划，例如学前班和启蒙计划。新墨西哥州官员表示，该计划必须扩大以满足需求。新墨西哥州观察到的问题也反映在全国各地，促使政策制定者和儿童保育倡导者密切关注该州的举措。
👶 根据左倾智库美国进步中心的数据，近一半的 5 岁及以下美国儿童生活在有执照的托儿沙漠中，那里供不应求。
👶 新墨西哥州的计划运营预算接近 6 亿美元，但一些立法者担心今年可能会超出预算 5000 万美元。
👶 新墨西哥州参议员史蒂夫·拉尼尔 (Steve Lanier) 告诉 NPR，该计划的高昂成本是他只支持为某些人提供全民托儿服务的原因，因为收入在 45 万或 60 万美元左右的人可能不需要援助。拉尼尔此前曾提起诉讼以终止该倡议，但诉讼未成功。
👶 自从新墨西哥州实行免费、全民托儿服务以来，低收入母亲取得了显着的进步。亚利桑那州立大学的一篇新论文显示，他们的全职就业人数增加了 23%。

title_en: Trump FDA nominee Heidi Overton struggling to win GOP support
title_zh: 特朗普 FDA 提名人海蒂·奥弗顿 (Heidi Overton) 努力赢得共和党支持
summary: Heidi Overton, Trump's pick to be FDA commissioner, is having trouble finding enough Republican support to advance her nomination, which could be pulled if she falls short.
summary_zh: 特朗普提名的 FDA 专员海蒂·奥弗顿 (Heidi Overton) 很难找到足够的共和党支持来推进她的提名，这可能会被取消
body_en: Dr. Heidi Overton, President Trump's pick to be FDA commissioner, is struggling to shore up enough support in the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee as it prepares to vote on her nomination Wednesday.

Sources tell CBS News that she's having trouble finding enough Republicans on the committee to vote to advance her nomination, which could be pulled if she can't muster the support. None of the Democrats on the committee are expected to back her.

The White House knows it has a problem, one source said, and has already begun looking for a new candidate. A second source confirmed that the White House has been talking to potential candidates, including some who could serve in an acting capacity and thus forgo Senate confirmation.
CBS News has reached out to the White House for comment.

Overton's nomination has run aground over her testimony regarding the FDA-approved chemical abortion drug mifepristone and her execution of President Trump's pro-vaping policies while she served on the Domestic Policy Council.

Missouri Republican Sen. Josh Hawley has emerged as one of the skeptics. Overton sidestepped questions on how she would handle a safety study long promised by the Trump administration into mifepristone, which Hawley has pressed for as well. The anti-abortion group Susan B. Anthony urged the Senate to delay her confirmation, and wants the FDA to commit to banning mail orders of mifepristone.

And two pro-abortion-access Republicans on the committee — Sens. Susan Collins of Maine and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska — have also not said whether they'll vote to advance her nomination. During Overton's confirmation hearing, Murkowski asked her whether she would restrict mifepristone , which is used in more than half of abortions in the U.S.

The administration has spoken with candidates about taking the FDA commissioner role in an acting capacity. That's one route to avoiding the Senate confirmation process during the narrow three-week legislative window ahead. The FDA oversees products that account for roughly 20% of consumer spending.
Two sources indicated Sen. Roger Marshall of Kansas, a doctor, is making a play for the FDA post. He lost his reelection bid to Democrat Adam Hamilton earlier this month.
Overton is arguably the Trump nominee with the highest profile who is struggling to shore up sufficient support in the closing weeks of GOP congressional control.

On Tuesday, Hung Cao, Mr. Trump's pick to serve as secretary of the Navy, faced a bipartisan grilling over his management of wartime operations and the Pentagon's decision to block Democrats from some classified military briefings. And retiring North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis said Tuesday he opposes the nomination of Eric Ueland, currently the deputy director of the Office of Management and Budget, to lead the Government Accountability Office, because of the involvement of Ueland and OMB in implementing DOGE cuts .

The FDA has been helmed by acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas since the last Senate-confirmed chief, Marty Makary , was forced out by the White House last spring. Multiple sources familiar with his ouster told CBS News that ongoing White House pressure over flavored vapes caused significant friction.

Dr. Makary told CBS News in a statement on Nov. 8 that "big tobacco exploited their connections to administration and HHS officials to put repeated pressure on me to approve fruit-flavored vapes that appeal to children – I wouldn't do it."
Mr. Trump campaigned in 2024 on a promise to save vaping, a smoking alternative that can help with breaking the smoking habit, but also has been found to have serious health side effects.

CBS News' "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" asked outgoing HELP Chairman Sen. Bill Cassidy, Republican of Louisiana, about whether Republicans would be able to install a Senate-confirmed FDA commissioner in these last weeks that they control the Senate. He raised the concern that the alternative would mean installing acting commissioners.

"Do we want a series of short-term administrators who probably will have more influence from the secretary, as opposed to someone who may be not, you know, the perfect candidate in somebody's mind, but at least would be a permanent one and have the ability to establish some independence. And that's part of the thought process there. That weighs on one side, and of course other things weigh on the other," Cassidy said Sunday.

Asked by "Face the Nation" about his own past remarks that Overton's association with Mr. Trump's efforts around reducing childhood vaccine uptake was "almost disqualifying," Cassidy acknowledged he was still working the phones and uncertain about whether Overton's nomination would be advanced by the HELP Committee he chairs, and he also did not say which way he would vote.

Overton stood beside Mr. Trump in the Oval Office as he signed an executive order on vaccines this summer — and the president twice erroneously referred to the measles or MMR vaccine as "lethal." None of the health officials present corrected Mr. Trump.

Recently resigned MAHA leader Calley Means, a former top adviser to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has also urged his followers to help block Overton's confirmation. He told "Face the Nation," "Heidi Overton was the biggest block to MAHA policies I encountered in the government."

Defenders of Overton dismissed criticism of her compliance with Mr. Trump's policies, and point to her medical background and her endorsement by two former FDA commissioners as a sign that she will be a professional.
body_zh: 特朗普总统提名的 FDA 专员海蒂·奥弗顿 (Heidi Overton) 博士正努力在参议院健康、教育、劳工和养老金委员会中争取足够的支持，该委员会正准备于周三对她的提名进行投票。
消息人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，她在委员会中很难找到足够的共和党人来投票推进她的提名，如果她不能获得支持，提名可能会被取消。预计委员会中的民主党人都不会支持她。
一位消息人士称，白宫知道自己遇到了问题，并已经开始寻找新的候选人。第二位消息人士证实，白宫一直在与潜在候选人进行谈判，其中包括一些可能以代理身份任职、从而放弃参议院确认的候选人。
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻已联系白宫征求评论。
奥弗顿的提名因她有关 FDA 批准的化学堕胎药物米非司酮的证词以及她在国内政策委员会任职期间执行特朗普总统支持电子烟的政策而搁浅。
密苏里州共和党参议员乔什·霍利 (Josh Hawley) 已成为怀疑者之一。奥弗顿回避了有关她将如何处理特朗普政府长期以来承诺的米非司酮安全研究的问题，霍利也一直敦促进行这项研究。反堕胎组织苏珊·B·安东尼 (Susan B. Anthony) 敦促参议院推迟对她的确认，并希望 FDA 承诺禁止米非司酮的邮购。
该委员会中两位支持堕胎的共和党人——缅因州参议员苏珊·柯林斯(Susan Collins)和阿拉斯加州参议员丽莎·穆尔科斯基(Lisa Murkowski)——也没有表示是否会投票支持她的提名。在奥弗顿的确认听证会上，穆尔科斯基问她是否会限制米非司酮的使用，美国一半以上的堕胎都使用米非司酮。
政府已与候选人讨论以代理身份担任 FDA 专员一职。这是在未来三周的狭窄立法窗口内避免参议院确认程序的一种途径。 FDA 监管的产品约占消费者支出的 20%。
两名消息人士称，堪萨斯州参议员罗杰·马歇尔（Roger Marshall）是一名医生，他正在竞选 FDA 职位。本月早些时候，他在连任竞选中输给了民主党人亚当·汉密尔顿。
奥弗顿可以说是最引人注目的特朗普提名人，他正在努力在共和党控制国会的最后几周内获得足够的支持。
周二，特朗普提名的海军部长曹洪因战时行动管理以及五角大楼决定阻止民主党人参加一些机密军事简报会而面临两党质询。即将退休的北卡罗来纳州共和党参议员汤姆·蒂利斯(Thom Tillis)周二表示，他反对提名现任管理和预算办公室副主任埃里克·尤兰(Eric Ueland)领导政府问责办公室，因为尤兰和OMB参与了DOGE削减的实施。
自去年春天上任参议院确认的局长马蒂·马卡里 (Marty Makary) 被白宫驱逐以来，FDA 一直由代理局长凯尔·迪亚曼塔斯 (Kyle Diamantas) 领导。多位熟悉他被罢免的消息人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，白宫在调味电子烟问题上持续施压，造成了巨大的摩擦。
马卡里博士在 11 月 8 日的一份声明中告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，“大型烟草公司利用他们与政府和卫生与公众服务部官员的关系，不断向我施压，要求我批准吸引儿童的水果味电子烟——我不会这样做。”
特朗普在 2024 年竞选时承诺拯救电子烟，电子烟是一种吸烟替代品，有助于戒烟，但也被发现具有严重的健康副作用。
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻节目《与玛格丽特·布伦南一起面对全国》向即将离任的 HELP 主席、路易斯安那州共和党参议员比尔·卡西迪询问共和党是否能够在他们控制参议院的最后几周内任命一位经参议院确认的 FDA 专员。他担心替代方案将意味着任命代理专员。
卡西迪周日表示：“我们是否想要一系列短期行政人员，他们可能会受到国务卿的更大影响，而不是那些可能不是某些人心目中的完美候选人，但至少会是永久性的，并有能力建立一定独立性的人。这是思考过程的一部分。这是一方面的压力，当然其他事情也会影响另一方面。”
在被《面对全国》问及他自己过去的言论时，卡西迪承认，他仍在打电话，不确定他所主持的帮助委员会是否会推进奥弗顿的提名，他也没有透露他将投票哪种方式。
今年夏天，当特朗普在椭圆形办公室签署一项有关疫苗的行政命令时，奥弗顿站在特朗普旁边，总统两次错误地将麻疹或 MMR 疫苗称为“致命的”。在场的卫生官员都没有纠正特朗普先生的说法。
最近辞职的 MAHA 领导人卡利·米恩斯 (Calley Means) 是卫生与公共服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.) 的前高级顾问，他也敦促他的追随者帮助阻止奥弗顿的确认。他告诉“面对国家”节目，“海蒂·奥弗顿是我在政府中遇到的 MAHA 政策的最大障碍。”
奥弗顿的捍卫者驳斥了对她遵守特朗普政策的批评，并指出她的医学背景和两位前 FDA 专员的支持表明她将成为一名专业人士。

title_en: First responders describe rescue efforts after New Orleans boat crash: ‘we have to save each other’
title_zh: 急救人员描述了新奥尔良船只失事后的救援工作：“我们必须互相拯救”
summary: More than 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River in mission being hailed as ‘Mississippi miracle’ Mariners and first responders who took part in the so-called “Mississippi miracle” rescue mission, which saw around 100 people pulled from the water af
summary_zh: 超过 100 人从密西西比河中被救起，此次任务被誉为“密西西比奇迹”
body_en: More than 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River in mission being hailed as ‘Mississippi miracle’

Mariners and first responders who took part in the so-called “Mississippi miracle” rescue mission, which saw about 100 people pulled from the water after a tanker collided with a cruise ship, have said they are thankful “everything came out all right”.
The collision on Friday between the Atlantic Asphalt tanker and the American Heritage riverboat saw more than 30 people injured.
Speaking days after the incident, responders told how they heard screams coming from inside the rooms of the sinking vessel, before they were able to free those onboard and bring them to safety.
William Brunner, the captain-on-watch of the nearby Madison Stone tow boat across the cruise ship, told Fox8 he initially heard the tanker’s distress call on his radio.
US officials recover audio from ‘Mississippi miracle’ cruise ship and tanker crash

“The only one that could get there fast enough was a tow boat,” Brunner said. When the ship began to capsize, Brunner said the Madison Stone pushed against it to keep it from moving while his five-person crew started to rescue the passengers.
“We had the only spot that [could] get close enough to get people off,” Brunner said. “We live out here on the water and we know that we have to save each other,” he added.
Captain Ryan Williams, who helped develop a rescue plan in the heat of the moment, told the outlet: “No 1 goal was to get everybody out.”

Williams told of how he and several other crew members began to hoist passengers off the cruise ship and on to the tow boat once they were within reach. “We heard screaming coming down from … a hole out of one of the rooms and the glass was closed. It was four individuals in there and we [were] able to get them out,” Williams said.
In total, the tug boat crew managed to rescue 27 people off the cruise ship.

Among the first responders who were also quick to the scene were more than 60 New Orleans firefighters. Varrick Dyer, captain of the New Orleans fire department’s hazardous materials unit, told WWLTV: “We train constantly. As a matter of fact, before we went on that water rescue, we had guys on the roof training doing rope rescue at that, like an hour before that incident happened.”

Dyer, whose crew is trained in rope skills, as well as rescues in water, elevators, high-rises and automobiles, said: “We [were] looking for the people who were injured the most, who couldn’t move, couldn’t swim or couldn’t help themselves.”

Many of the passengers were seniors using wheelchairs or crutches, who were unable to use the firefighters’ rescue ladders. Fortunately, they managed to disembark via a gangway connecting the cruise ship to the dock before the ship then capsized and began to sink.

The fire department’s captain, Grant Rodriguez, told the outlet: “We did not have a lot of time. It went quick. The gangway went. The boat then retracted very hard to the rear. It then pushed away from the wharf all at the same moment … As it rolled, there was a lot of panic. It was cold, people were shivering. The river was extremely cold.”
Melanie Montroll, chief of the the New Orleans Harbor police, who were also on the scene, detailed the moment she ordered two officers on to the vessel as it began to capsize.

“Looking two officers in the face and sending them into a no-win situation, knowing what the potential outcome would be, it’s tough,” Montroll told Nola.com , adding: “I know my officers. I know their families. I know their kids.”

After the rescues, Montroll waded into the river to pull out the two injured officers, one of whom could not stand. “My goal was, one, to make sure that we got as many people, but two that I didn’t leave my officers in the water. That was a big concern of mine. I made that decision to put them on there, but we don’t leave our own,” Montroll told Nola.com .

Amid the rescue operations, the captain of the cruise ship, Leonard Stewart, remained on the bridge as the vessel capsized, repeatedly calling for help and keeping the boat by the dock so everyone else could disembark safely.
body_zh: 100多人从密西西比河中被救起，此次任务被誉为“密西西比奇迹”
参与所谓“密西西比奇迹”救援任务的海员和急救人员表示，他们很庆幸“一切顺利”。在这次救援任务中，一艘油轮与一艘游轮相撞，约 100 人被从水中救出。
周五，Atlantic Asphalt 油轮与 American Heritage 河船发生碰撞，造成 30 多人受伤。
事件发生几天后，救援人员讲述了他们如何听到沉船房间内传来尖叫声，然后他们才将船上的人救出并带至安全地带。
游轮附近麦迪逊斯通拖船的值班船长威廉·布伦纳 (William Brunner) 告诉 Fox8，他最初在无线电中听到了油轮的求救信号。
美国官员从“密西西比奇迹”游轮和油轮事故中恢复了音频
“唯一能够足够快地到达那里的是一艘拖船，”布伦纳说。布伦纳说，当船开始倾覆时，麦迪逊斯通号推力阻止其移动，同时他的五名船员开始营救乘客。
“我们有唯一一个可以足够近让人们下车的地方，”布伦纳说。 “我们生活在水面上，我们知道我们必须互相拯救，”他补充道。
瑞安·威廉姆斯上尉在最紧张的时刻帮助制定了救援计划，他告诉媒体：“我们的首要目标是让所有人都逃出来。”
威廉姆斯讲述了他和其他几名船员如何在乘客触手可及的情况下开始将乘客从游轮上吊到拖船上。 “我们听到尖叫声从其中一个房间的一个洞里传来，而且玻璃是关闭的。里面有四个人，我们能够把他们救出来，”威廉姆斯说。
拖船船员总共成功救出了游轮上的 27 人。
60 多名新奥尔良消防员也迅速赶到现场。新奥尔良消防局危险材料小组队长瓦里克·戴尔 (Varrick Dyer) 告诉 WWLTV：“我们不断进行训练。事实上，在我们进行水上救援之前，我们已经让人员在屋顶上进行了绳索救援训练，大约是在事件发生前一个小时。”
戴尔的船员接受过绳索技能以及水中、电梯、高层建筑和汽车救援方面的培训，他说：“我们正在寻找受伤最严重、无法移动、不会游泳或无法自救的人。”
许多乘客都是使用轮椅或拐杖的老年人，他们无法使用消防员的救援梯。幸运的是，他们设法通过连接游轮和码头的舷梯下船，然后游轮倾覆并开始下沉。
消防队队长格兰特·罗德里格斯（Grant Rodriguez）告诉媒体：“我们没有太多时间。时间很快。舷梯消失了。然后船非常用力地向后缩回。然后它同时从码头上推开……当它滚动时，有很多恐慌。天气很冷，人们瑟瑟发抖。河水非常冷。”
新奥尔良港警察局长梅兰妮·蒙特罗尔也在现场，她详细介绍了当船只开始倾覆时她命令两名警察上岸的那一刻。
蒙特罗尔告诉 Nola.com：“直视两名警官，让他们陷入双赢的境地，知道潜在的结果是什么，这很艰难。”他补充道：“我了解我的警官。我了解他们的家人。我了解他们的孩子。”
救援结束后，蒙特罗尔涉入河中救出两名受伤警官，其中一名警官无法站立。 “我的目​​标是，第一，确保我们有尽可能多的人，但第二，我不让我的军官留在水中。这是我的一个大问题。我决定把他们放在那里，但我们不会留下我们自己的人，”蒙特罗尔告诉 Nola.com。
在救援行动中，游轮倾覆时，船长伦纳德·斯图尔特 (Leonard Stewart) 留在桥上，反复呼救，并将船停在码头附近，以便其他人都能安全下船。

title_en: Man convicted in Iran-backed plot to kill Trump is sentenced
title_zh: 因伊朗支持密谋刺杀特朗普而被定罪的男子被判刑
summary: A man who was convicted of attempted terrorism and murder-for-hire plots, with potential targets including President Trump and former President Joe Biden, was sentenced to 27 1/2 years in federal prison.
summary_zh: 一名因恐怖主义未遂和雇佣谋杀阴谋而被定罪的男子，潜在目标包括特朗普总统和前总统乔·毕
body_en: A Pakistani man who was convicted of attempted terrorism and orchestrating a murder-for-hire plot at the direction of Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps, with potential targets including President Trump and former President Joe Biden, was sentenced to 27 1/2 years in federal prison on Tuesday.

Asif Merchant was convicted in March — shortly after the start of the Iran war — on terrorism and murder-for-hire charges and faced up to life in prison. Merchant shuffled into court with a serious expression and shackled ankles, peering around the room. He had wavy gray hair and wore a tan prison outfit. He pressed a headphone to his ear, for an Urdu translation of the proceedings, watching the judge intently and bobbing in his chair as he learned his fate.

"This was an exceptionally severe crime, an extreme instance of terroristic violence," said Brooklyn-based U.S. District Judge Eric R. Komitee, a Trump appointee. "No crimes are more serious than the targeted killing of a U.S. president or other U.S. officials."

Komitee called the "overlay of foreign influence" from Iran an aggravating factor, noting that Iran is the largest state sponsor of terrorism in the world. "The conduct we see here is not an isolated episode for that foreign actor," he said.

Merchant was accused of traveling to the United States to recruit criminal associates and hire hit men to carry out his scheme. The plot involved the assassination of a politician, stealing documents from a target's home and arranging a protest as a distraction after the murder occurred, according to court documents.
He was charged with one count of attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and one count of murder for hire.

He testified in his own defense during the trial, and admitted that he had been recruited by a member of the Revolutionary Guard Corps, Iran's elite military branch that answers to the supreme leader. In addition to Mr. Trump and Biden, he testified that former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley was also a potential target of the plot.

To carry out the plot, Merchant reached out to a contact in the U.S. for assistance, but that person turned out to be a confidential source working with law enforcement. That confidential source, known by the pseudonym Nadeem Ali, ultimately connected Merchant with two alleged hit men who were actually undercover FBI agents. He paid them $5,000 each as down payments for the assassinations.

On the stand, Merchant claimed that he carried out the plot under duress, out of fear his wife and child in Iran would be harmed if he didn't comply. Merchant also has a wife and children in Pakistan. Prosecutors disputed his claim, saying there was no evidence that he had "fear for relatives." Iran has denied plotting to kill Mr. Trump or other high-ranking U.S. officials.

During sentencing, Komitee said the evidence was clear that Merchant was "highly motivated himself to do harm to this country." He said it was possible Merchant had some concern for his family's well-being in Iran, but did not accept the defense's characterization that was the sole motivation behind his actions.
The government pointed to Merchant's own social media posts as evidence, including a post of Mr. Trump's severed head with the words "coming soon" and "severe revenge."
According to trial exhibits, Merchant had searched for Trump campaign rally locations in 2024 and searched the address of at least one rally on Google Maps.

As a front for the plot, Merchant set up a garment business, and used terms related to articles of clothing as code words to communicate about the plan. He instructed the confidential source, who he thought was his associate, that "T-shirt" meant protest, "flannel shirt" meant stealing and "fleece jacket" was to "commit the act of the game," indicating murder.

Merchant's lawyer Christopher Neff disputed that the garment business was a front during sentencing, calling it a real business. The prosecution pointed to a video of Merchant, played at trial, in which he told Ali that "the goal is not to make a profit, the goal is to launder money for the IRGC murder plot."

Neff told the judge that Merchant's plot was "never particularly likely to succeed," since the IRGC sent him to "kill a politician with Secret Service protection and extraordinarily tight security yet gave him almost no resources to carry it out."
"Mr. Merchant is simply not the monster that the government would like you to believe," said Neff. "He is an ordinary guy."
The government countered that the plot was "not farfetched … it was straight out of the IRGC playbook."
Merchant was arrested on July 12, 2024, the day before the attempted assassination of Mr. Trump in Butler, Pennsylvania.
When Merchant was told about the Butler assassination attempt, he responded that what occurred at the rally was "the same thing he was sent here to do."

As the sentencing ended, Komitee wished Merchant the best, telling him: "No matter how serious the crimes of conviction, no human is to be judged entirely by the biggest mistakes they've made in their lives."
body_zh: 一名巴基斯坦男子被判犯有恐怖主义未遂罪，并在伊朗革命卫队的指导下策划雇佣谋杀阴谋，潜在目标包括特朗普总统和前总统乔·拜登，周二被判处在联邦监狱服刑 27.5 年。
伊朗战争爆发后不久，阿西夫·麦昌特 (Asif Merchant) 在 3 月份被判犯有恐怖主义和雇佣谋杀罪，最高可判处终身监禁。麦钱特戴着脚镣，拖着脚步走进法庭，表情严肃，环顾四周。他有一头卷曲的灰色头发，穿着棕褐色的囚服。他把耳机贴在耳边，聆听乌尔都语翻译，他专注地看着法官，在椅子上摇晃着，了解自己的命运。
特朗普任命的布鲁克林美国地区法官埃里克·R·科米蒂（Eric R. Komitee）表示：“这是一起极其严重的犯罪行为，是恐怖暴力的极端实例。” “没有比针对美国总统或其他美国官员的定点杀害更严重的犯罪行为了。”
委员会称伊朗的“外国影响力叠加”是一个加剧因素，并指出伊朗是世界上最大的恐怖主义支持国家。 “我们在这里看到的行为对于该外国演员来说并不是一个孤立的事件，”他说。
麦钱特被指控前往美国招募犯罪同伙并雇用杀手来实施他的计划。法庭文件显示，该阴谋涉及暗杀一名政客、从目标家中窃取文件，并在谋杀发生后安排抗议活动以分散注意力。
他被指控一项企图实施超越国界的恐怖主义行为和一项雇佣谋杀罪。
他在审判期间为自己辩护作证，并承认自己是由革命卫队的一名成员招募的，革命卫队是伊朗的精英军事部门，听命于最高领袖。他作证说，除了特朗普和拜登之外，前联合国大使尼基·黑利也是该阴谋的潜在目标。
为了实施这一阴谋，麦钱特联系了美国的一位联系人寻求帮助，但事实证明该人是与执法部门合作的机密消息来源。这位化名纳迪姆·阿里的机密消息人士最终将麦钱特与两名涉嫌杀手联系起来，而这两名杀手实际上是联邦调查局卧底特工。他向他们每人支付了 5,000 美元作为暗杀的预付款。
麦钱特在证人席上声称，他是在胁迫下实施这一阴谋的，因为他担心如果他不服从，他在伊朗的妻子和孩子会受到伤害。商人在巴基斯坦也有妻子和孩子。检察官对他的说法提出异议，称没有证据表明他“害怕亲戚”。伊朗否认密谋刺杀特朗普或其他美国高级官员。
在宣判期间，委员会表示，证据明确表明麦钱特“自己有强烈的动机去伤害这个国家”。他说，麦钱特可能对他在伊朗的家人的福祉有些担忧，但不接受辩方的描述，这是他行为背后的唯一动机。
政府以麦钱特自己的社交媒体帖子作为证据，其中包括一张特朗普被砍下头颅的帖子，上面写着“即将到来”和“严厉报复”。
根据审判证据，麦钱特曾搜索过 2024 年特朗普竞选集会地点，并在谷歌地图上搜索了至少一场集会的地址。
作为剧情的幌子，麦钱特开设了一家服装公司，并使用与服装相关的术语作为暗语来传达该计划。他告诉这位他认为是他的同事的机密消息来源，“T恤”意味着抗议，“法兰绒衬衫”意味着偷窃，“羊毛夹克”意味着“实施游戏行为”，表示谋杀。
麦钱特的律师克里斯托弗·内夫（Christopher Neff）在量刑期间对服装业务是幌子的说法提出异议，称其为真正的业务。检方指出，麦钱特在庭审时播放了一段视频，视频中他告诉阿里，“我们的目标不是盈利，而是为伊斯兰革命卫队的谋杀阴谋洗钱。”
内夫告诉法官，麦钱特的阴谋“从来都不太可能成功”，因为伊斯兰革命卫队派他去“在特勤局的保护和极其严密的安全保护下杀死一名政客，但却几乎没有给他提供任何资源来实施这一行动”。
“麦钱特先生根本不是政府希望你相信的怪物，”内夫说。 “他是一个普通人。”
政府反驳说，这一阴谋“并不牵强……它直接出自伊斯兰革命卫队的剧本”。
麦钱特于 2024 年 7 月 12 日被捕，就在特朗普先生在宾夕法尼亚州巴特勒遭到暗杀的前一天。
当麦钱特被告知巴特勒刺杀企图时，他回答说，集会上发生的事情“和他被派到这里去做的事情是一样的”。
宣判结束时，委员会祝愿麦钱特一切顺利，并告诉他：“无论定罪的罪行有多么严重，任何人都不能完全根据他们一生中犯下的最大错误来接受审判。”

title_en: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip
title_zh: 特朗普抵达菲律宾开启亚洲之行
summary: Manila is President Trump's first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
summary_zh: 马尼拉是特朗普总统为期三天的访问的第一站，随后他将前往中国与中国国家主席进行历史性的三方核会谈
body_en: Trump arrives in Philippines Manila is President Trump's first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

President Donald Trump inspects an honor guard after stepping off Air Force One, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila, Philippines. Mark Schiefelbein/AP hide caption

MANILA, Philippines — President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday, where he was scheduled to meet regional partners, talk trade, and seek a break from a series of setbacks at home, ranging from a major disruption to the U.S. aviation industry to a scandal that has shaken the global AI industry.
Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout

Manila, the Philippine capital, is Trump's first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and, according to Trump, potentially for a meeting with North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un.

The visit marks Trump's first travel abroad since his party suffered deep losses in midterm elections. The White House and stock market alike have been rattled by the departure of Jensen Huang from Nvidia last week after admitting to an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent. Beijing has said it was not involved.

As he descended the stairs from Air Force One, Trump pumped his fist. A child handed him small American and Philippine flags, which Trump waved and then swooped in big circular motions as he smiled. The U.S. president was greeted by a marching band playing "YMCA" while he walked to a waiting helicopter.

Trump's first hours in the Philippines will include all the reassuring optics from Washington's oldest treaty ally in Asia, including a cocktail reception and dinner with other world leaders, an intermission from some of the thorniest issues at home. He's being feted Tuesday night at a gala as the "guest of honor" at the annual summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

The ASEAN leaders have been working on a non-aggression pact with China in the contested waters of the South China Sea, a key global trade route. Confrontations have escalated in recent years, particularly between Chinese and Philippine coast guard and naval forces in disputed shoals.

First on Trump's agenda Tuesday is a meeting with the leaders of the Quad nations, comprising the U.S., Australia, India, and Japan that have aimed to counter China's influence in the Asia Pacific. It will be their first meeting since Trump returned to the White House last year.
Trump is then scheduled to sign a trade deal with Thailand, the type of agreement he has relished striking since launching a trade war last year buttressed by steep tariff threats.

The U.S. had announced a trade framework last October in which Thailand would remove tariffs on most American goods, as well as barriers for importing U.S. autos, food products and pharmaceutical drugs, according to the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative. At the time, the Trump administration said Thailand would also spend more than $18 billion on U.S. aircraft and buy U.S. farm goods and liquefied natural gas.

The U.S. Supreme Court overturned in February the 19% tariff that Trump placed on goods from Thailand. The administration sought replacement tariffs in July by levying a 12.5% tax on imports from Thailand for not taking steps to oppose the use of forced labor.

Before the gala dinner Tuesday night, Trump will participate in what's billed as a "special summit" with the ASEAN leaders, where they are expected to discuss efforts to deepen trade and security ties as well as the region's longstanding conflicts, including yearslong violence in Myanmar and escalating disputes in the South China Sea, which Beijing claims virtually in its entirety.
Washington rejects China's expansive claim in the waterway, and has repeatedly stated that it's obligated to defend the Philippines if Filipino forces come under an armed attack.

Demonstrators hold signs during a protest against U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to attend the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit and related meetings in Manila, Philippines, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Firdia Linsawati/AP hide caption
About 1,500 left-wing protesters held a noisy rally in a downtown Manila square ahead of Trump's arrival, calling on Philippine leaders not to take their foreign policy cues from the U.S.
They waved red flags and held up a large streamer that read, "Resist U.S. war and plunder!" They planned to burn an effigy of Trump. Riot police with shields and wooden truncheons stood nearby.

"The Philippine government should not deal with such a loser so our call to the Marcos administration is to stop being a puppet of Donald Trump and to uphold an independent foreign policy for the Philippines," protest leader Teddy Casiño told The Associated Press at the Liwasang Bonifacio square, referring to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
body_zh: 特朗普抵达菲律宾 马尼拉是特朗普总统为期三天的访问的第一站，随后他将前往中国与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京进行历史性的三方核会谈。
2026 年 11 月 17 日星期二，唐纳德·特朗普总统在菲律宾马尼拉尼诺·阿基诺国际机场走下空军一号后检阅仪仗队。马克·希费尔贝因/美联社隐藏标题栏
菲律宾马尼拉——唐纳德·特朗普总统周二抵达菲律宾，他计划在那里会见地区合作伙伴，讨论贸易问题，并寻求摆脱国内一系列挫折，从对美国航空业的重大破坏到震动全球人工智能行业的丑闻。
在英伟达的影响下，特朗普前往亚洲会见习近平和普京
菲律宾首都马尼拉是特朗普为期三天的访问的第一站，随后他将前往中国与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京进行历史性的三方核会谈，据特朗普称，可能还会与朝鲜领导人金正恩会面。
此次访问是特朗普自其政党在中期选举中惨败以来首次出国访问。黄仁勋上周离开英伟达，此前他承认与一名所谓的中国政府特工有染，这让白宫和股市都感到不安。北京方面表示没有参与其中。
当特朗普从空军一号走下楼梯时，他挥动了拳头。一个孩子递给他一些小美国和菲律宾国旗，特朗普挥舞着这些国旗，然后微笑着以大圆圈的方式猛扑过去。当美国总统走向一架等待的直升机时，演奏着“基督教青年会”的游行乐队迎接了他。
特朗普在菲律宾的头几个小时将包括来自华盛顿在亚洲最古老的条约盟友的所有令人放心的镜头，包括与其他世界领导人的鸡尾酒会和晚宴，以及国内一些最棘手问题的间歇。周二晚上，他作为东南亚国家联盟年度峰会的“主宾”在一场盛会上受到招待。
东盟领导人一直致力于在南海争议海域与中国签订互不侵犯条约，南海是全球重要的贸易路线。近年来，对抗不断升级，特别是中国和菲律宾海岸警卫队和海军部队在争议浅滩上的对抗。
特朗普周二的首要议程是与四国领导人举行会议，这些国家包括美国、澳大利亚、印度和日本，旨在对抗中国在亚太地区的影响力。这将是特朗普去年重返白宫以来他们的首次会面。
特朗普随后计划与泰国签署一项贸易协议，自去年在严厉的关税威胁的支持下发起贸易战以来，他一直很喜欢达成这样的协议。
据美国贸易代表办公室称，美国去年10月宣布了一项贸易框架，泰国将取消对大多数美国商品的关税，以及进口美国汽车、食品和药品的壁垒。当时，特朗普政府表示，泰国还将花费超过180亿美元购买美国飞机，并购买美国农产品和液化天然气。
美国最高法院二月份推翻了特朗普对泰国商品征收的 19% 关税。由于没有采取措施反对使用强迫劳动，政府于 7 月寻求替代关税，对来自泰国的进口产品征收 12.5% 的税。
在周二晚上的晚宴之前，特朗普将参加与东盟领导人举行的所谓“特别峰会”，预计他们将在会上讨论深化贸易和安全关系的努力以及该地区长期存在的冲突，包括缅甸多年的暴力和南海不断升级的争端，北京对南海几乎拥有全部主权。
华盛顿拒绝中国在该航道的广泛主权主张，并多次表示，如果菲律宾军队受到武装攻击，美国有义务保卫菲律宾。
2026 年 11 月 17 日星期二，示威者举着标语抗议美国总统唐纳德·特朗普前往菲律宾马尼拉参加第 49 届东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 峰会及相关会议。Firdia Linsawati/美联社隐藏标题栏
在特朗普抵达之前，约 1,500 名左翼抗议者在马尼拉市中心广场举行了喧闹的集会，呼吁菲律宾领导人不要听从美国的外交政策暗示。
他们挥舞着红旗，举着写着“抵制美国战争和掠夺！”的大横幅。他们计划焚烧特朗普的肖像。附近站着手持盾牌和木警棍的防暴警察。
抗议领袖泰迪·卡西诺在利瓦桑博尼法西奥广场对美联社表示：“菲律宾政府不应该与这样的失败者打交道，因此我们呼吁马科斯政府停止成为唐纳德·特朗普的傀儡，并维护菲律宾的独立外交政策。”

title_en: Sean Duffy’s $50 billion demand for air travel fixes is met with yelling and skepticism in Congress
title_zh: 肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 提出的 500 亿美元航空旅行修复需求遭到了国会的叫喊和怀疑
summary: The Trump administration’s request for $50.1 billion in new FAA funding after a nationwide ground stop is running into skepticism from both parties in Congress.
summary_zh: 特朗普政府在全国范围内停飞后请求美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 提供 501 亿美元的新资金，这一请求遭到了两党的怀疑。
body_en: Nov. 17, 2026, 5:51 PM EST / Updated Nov. 17, 2026, 6:06 PM EST
By Patrick Maguire , Sahil Kapur and Julie Tsirkin

WASHINGTON — The Trump administration’s request for $50.1 billion in new Federal Aviation Administration funding after a nationwide ground stop strangled air travel is running into skepticism from both parties on Capitol Hill.
The funding request was suddenly increased from $30 billion after the hourslong ground stop Friday caused delays and cancellations for passengers across thousands of flights.

The formal funding ask was conveyed in a Tuesday letter signed by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who refused to apologize or accept responsibility for the failure, blaming it on predecessors and Congress. The letter, cosigned by FAA chief Bryan Bedford and White House budget director Russell Vought, stated the money was needed “to deliver a truly world-class air traffic control network.”
After publicly reproaching Congress for the failure last week, Duffy met privately with Senate Republicans on Tuesday to make his case on Capitol Hill.
Secretary Duffy calls for air traffic control upgrades after meeting lawmakers

The closed-door briefing was contentious. The transportation secretary was “yelled at” by multiple Republican senators during his briefing, according to a person in the room who was not authorized to speak publicly about the private discussion.
When it was over, Senate Republican leaders and Duffy notably held their news conferences separately.
Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., stopped short of endorsing the full funding figure, saying only that the GOP is unified around the belief that “safe skies is an incredibly important priority.”
“We will see what the traffic will bear, what’s achievable,” he said, calling it a “discussion to be had” on the dollar amount.
Duffy met with only Republicans on Tuesday, not Democrats — even though the regular government funding process requires bipartisan support.

And Democrats were left wanting a better explanation, particularly as Duffy has pointed fingers at them. And members in both parties noted that President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” included $12.5 billion for air traffic control that still has not been fully used up.

“Look, we have not been given the answers. They have not come clean,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., told reporters on Tuesday. “At his first press conference, all Duffy did was attack Democrats, and he asked for $50 billion when they haven’t even spent the $12 billion we’ve given to them. I have little faith in them.”
Facing Republican questions on the matter, Duffy insisted that the $12.5 billion was insufficient for the specific upgrades he deemed necessary in this situation.
Other Democrats are vexed by the FAA funding request.

“I generally support the idea of investing in air traffic control, but $50 billion sounds like an awfully round number,” said Sen. Brian Schatz, D-Hawaii, who’s poised to become majority whip and also sits on the Senate Appropriations Committee.

The issue is wrapped up in a larger debate about funding the government ahead of a Dec. 11 deadline to avoid another shutdown . Congress could either reach a deal by then on new funding, punt it to next year with a stopgap bill, or fail to act and allow a shutdown.
Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, said air traffic control is “absolutely not a partisan issue” and that Congress will work to make sure that any funding is “paid for in a responsible way.”

Republicans are also considering a party-line “reconciliation” bill to approve military funding without the need for Democratic votes; Democrats are likely to resist additional military funds unless the Iran war comes to an end. Other provisions could be added to such a bill — if it materializes before Republicans lose control of Congress. Thune indicated Tuesday that it is still an open question, as Republicans would need to pass a budget resolution by Thanksgiving to pull it off. It would be a long, arduous process requiring near-total GOP unity in both chambers, and it would need to begin soon in order to finish this year.
body_zh: 美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 17 日下午 5:51 / 更新于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 17 日下午 6:06
作者：帕特里克·马奎尔、萨希尔·卡普尔和朱莉·齐尔金
华盛顿——在全国范围内的地面停止阻碍了航空旅行之后，特朗普政府请求联邦航空管理局提供 501 亿美元的新资金，这一请求遭到了国会山两党的怀疑。
周五长达数小时的地面停留导致数千个航班延误和取消后，资金请求突然从 300 亿美元增加。
交通部长肖恩·达菲(Sean Duffy)周二签署了一封信，提出了正式的资金请求，达菲拒绝道歉或承担失败的责任，并将其归咎于前任和国会。这封信由美国联邦航空局局长布莱恩·贝德福德和白宫预算主管拉塞尔·沃特共同签署，信中表示需要这笔资金“以建立一个真正世界级的空中交通管制网络”。
在上周公开谴责国会的失败后，达菲于周二私下会见了参议院共和党人，在国会山阐述了他的观点。
达菲部长在会见立法者后呼吁升级空中交通管制
这次闭门简报会引起了争议。据房间内一位未获授权公开谈论私下讨论的人士称，交通部长在新闻发布会上遭到多位共和党参议员的“吼叫”。
会议结束后，参议院共和党领导人和达菲分别举行了新闻发布会。
多数党领袖约翰·图恩（R-S.D.）没有对全额资金数字表示认可，只是表示共和党一致相信“安全天空是极其重要的优先事项”。
“我们将看看交通将承受什么，可以实现什么，”他说，并称这是关于美元金额的“讨论”。
达菲周二只会见了共和党人，而不是民主党人——尽管常规的政府资助程序需要两党的支持。
民主党人希望得到更好的解释，尤其是在达菲指责他们的情况下。两党成员都指出，唐纳德·特朗普总统的“庞大而美丽的法案”包括用于空中交通管制的 125 亿美元，但尚未完全用完。
“看，我们还没有得到答案。他们还没有坦白，”纽约州参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默周二告诉记者。 “在他的第一次新闻发布会上，达菲所做的只是攻击民主党人，他要求提供 500 亿美元，而他们甚至还没有花掉我们给他们的 120 亿美元。我对他们没什么信心。”
面对共和党对此事的质疑，达菲坚称 125 亿美元不足以进行他认为在这种情况下必要的具体升级。
其他民主党人对美国联邦航空局的资助请求感到恼火。
“我总体上支持投资空中交通管制的想法，但 500 亿美元听起来是一个非常大的数字，”即将成为多数党党鞭、参议院拨款委员会成员的夏威夷州民主党参议员布赖恩·沙茨 (Brian Schatz) 说。
这个问题最终归结为一场更广泛的争论，争论的主题是在 12 月 11 日最后期限之前为政府提供资金，以避免再次关闭。国会要么届时就新资金达成协议，通过权宜法案将其推迟到明年，要么不采取行动并允许政府关门。
俄亥俄州共和党参议员伯尼·莫雷诺表示，空中交通管制“绝对不是党派问题”，国会将努力确保任何资金“以负责任的方式支付”。

共和党人还在考虑一项党派路线“和解”法案，以批准军事拨款，而无需民主党投票；除非伊朗战争结束，否则民主党人可能会抵制额外的军事资金。如果该法案在共和党失去国会控制权之前得以实现，则可以在该法案中添加其他条款。图恩周二表示，这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题，因为共和党需要在感恩节之前通过一项预算决议才能实现这一目标。这将是一个漫长而艰巨的过程，需要共和党在参众两院几乎完全团结，并且需要尽快开始才能在今年完成。

title_en: Democrats see an immigration opening despite Stephen Miller’s rise
title_zh: 尽管斯蒂芬·米勒崛起，民主党仍看到移民开放
summary: Several moderate Democrats have already placed calls to the White House and Trump administration officials to express a willingness to work together.
summary_zh: 一些温和的民主党人已经向白宫和特朗普政府官员发出呼吁，表达合作的意愿。
body_en: In the days before the midterm election, Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) felt confident that a blue wave could open the door to immigration reform.

Cuellar was so bullish that he reached out to acting Immigration and Customs Enforcement director David Venturella and the Customs and Border Protection commissioner Rodney Scott to feel out areas of “common ground,” he said in an interview.

Now Cuellar is one of several moderate Democrats angling to strike a deal with the White House, especially on reining in ICE officers and creating legal pathways to citizenship for some immigrants. They’re undeterred by President Donald Trump’s elevation of immigration hardliner Stephen Miller to chief of staff. And they’re buoyed by Trump’s recent admission that his deportations policy was “too tough.”

Several of these Democrats have already placed calls to Trump and DHS secretary Markwayne Mullin to express a willingness to work together. Cuellar said he reached back out to Venturella and Scott after the election to try to schedule meetings.

“If the president, as the president of the United States, makes a decision — and not a chief of staff — we can get the job done,” Cuellar said in an interview. “I’m sure we’re going to find a lot of differences, but if we sit down, we can definitely resolve them.”

It’ll be a tough road: Securing buy-in from the White House becomes undoubtedly more complicated with Miller, a champion of the administration’s aggressive deportation push. Republicans in Congress have largely been willing to defer to the president on the issue. And Democratic leaders have questioned Trump’s sincerity and said they have no interest in working with Miller.
The possibility will become even more tenuous once Democrats begin investigating the Trump administration, including the president’s immigration enforcement agencies.
CBP and ICE did not respond to requests for comment.
Neither did Democratic leaders Sen. Chuck Schumer and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries.

Democrats like Cuellar, Sen.-elects James Talarico of Texas and Annie Andrews of South Carolina are aware of all of those hurdles. But they’re betting the midterms have created an opening for serious talks: Latino voters across the country swung hard back toward Democrats this cycle, and more and more Republicans are recognizing that their immigration agenda hurt them politically.

Talarico and Andrews have publicly expressed interest in working with the president on immigration, and both ran on platforms that emphasized creating paths to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.
“I’m ready to work with President Trump to fix this broken immigration system,” Talarico said in a statement.

Inside the White House, there’s a recognition that the president will proceed however he so chooses, regardless of who the chief of staff is. Trump is accessible to outside voices — journalists, business leaders and lawmakers regularly call him directly — and often poses policy questions to aides and allies as he decides which direction he will go.

“Everybody’s like, ‘Well, it’s never going to happen with Stephen Miller.’ Look, Donald Trump’s the president. I don’t care if Stephen Miller’s the chief of staff or Susie Wiles or John Kelly or whoever the chief of staff might be,” said a person close to the White House, granted anonymity to speak about the internal dynamic.

For Democrats, there’s a real political incentive to getting a deal done ahead of a critical 2028 presidential election — especially as the party seeks to win back voter trust on immigration and border security, policy areas that spelled doom for them in 2024.

“You have these Democrats who flip red states, and it’s also to their self-interest, right? Not just to do rhetoric, and go big or go home, but actually come to the middle with the president, with the Republicans. Because if not, I think that the big lesson this election is, Hispanic voters are gonna flip back ... if they don’t see Democrats delivering anything the next two years,” said Rebecca Shi, the executive director of ABIC, a coalition of pro-immigration reform business executives.
She added that there’s a lesson for Republicans, too, if they don’t come to the table: “They will lose the White House.”

White House spokesperson Lauren Bis touted Trump’s immigration accomplishments, including border security, a drop in crime and the creation of the Homeland Security Task Force and said the president’s “strong immigration policy remains unchanged.”
She said Democrats should work alongside Trump to “keep our southern border secure, remove dangerous illegal criminals from our communities, and stop the illicit trafficking of lethal drugs.”

Democrats welcomed the president’s remarks on 60 Minutes on Sunday, when he said he was open to legal pathways for some unauthorized immigrants who haven’t committed crimes and are working and contributing to the economy. Mullin also floated an openness to a bipartisan immigration overhaul involving DACA, which could provide permanent legal status to some undocumented immigrants who arrived in the U.S. as children, even as he — and the president — have insisted that any proposal wouldn’t include amnesty.
body_zh: 在中期选举前几天，德克萨斯州民主党众议员亨利·奎利亚尔 (Henry Cuellar) 对蓝色浪潮能够打开移民改革的大门充满信心。
奎利亚尔在接受采访时表示，他非常乐观，以至于他联系了代理移民和海关执法局局长戴维·文图拉（David Venturella）以及海关和边境保护局局长罗德尼·斯科特（Rodney Scott），以找出“共同点”。
现在，奎利亚尔是几位试图与白宫达成协议的温和派民主党人之一，特别是在控制 ICE 官员和为一些移民创造获得公民身份的合法途径方面。唐纳德·特朗普总统任命移民强硬派斯蒂芬·米勒为幕僚长，但他们并没有被吓倒。特朗普最近承认他的驱逐政策“过于严厉”，这让他们受到鼓舞。
其中一些民主党人已经致电特朗普和国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林，表达了合作的意愿。奎利亚尔说，他在选举后再次联系了文琴拉和斯科特，试图安排会议。
“如果总统，作为美国总统，做出决定——而不是幕僚长——我们就能完成工作，”奎利亚尔在接受采访时说。 “我确信我们会发现很多分歧，但如果我们坐下来，我们绝对可以解决它们。”
这将是一条艰难的道路：对于米勒来说，获得白宫的支持无疑变得更加复杂，米勒是政府激进驱逐行动的支持者。国会中的共和党人基本上愿意在这个问题上听从总统的意见。民主党领导人质疑特朗普的诚意，并表示他们没有兴趣与米勒合作。
一旦民主党开始调查特朗普政府，包括总统的移民执法机构，这种可能性将变得更加渺茫。
CBP 和 ICE 没有回应置评请求。
民主党领袖参议员查克·舒默和众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯也没有。
奎利亚尔、德克萨斯州当选参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科和南卡罗来纳州安妮·安德鲁斯等民主党人都意识到所有这些障碍。但他们押注中期选举为严肃的谈判创造了机会：全国各地的拉丁裔选民在本轮选举中强力转向民主党，越来越多的共和党人认识到他们的移民议程在政治上伤害了他们。
塔拉里科和安德鲁斯公开表示有兴趣与总统在移民问题上合作，两人的竞选纲领都强调为无证移民创造获得公民身份的途径。
塔拉里科在一份声明中表示：“我已准备好与特朗普总统合作，修复这个破碎的移民体系。”
在白宫内部，人们认识到，无论幕僚长是谁，总统都将按照他的选择行事。特朗普很容易听到外界的声音——记者、商界领袖和立法者经常直接给他打电话——并且在决定自己的发展方向时经常向助手和盟友提出政策问题。
“每个人都会说，‘嗯，史蒂芬·米勒永远不会发生这样的事。’瞧，唐纳德·特朗普是总统。我不在乎史蒂芬·米勒是幕僚长、苏西·怀尔斯、约翰·凯利还是其他人，”一位不愿透露姓名的白宫人士在谈到内部动态时表示。
对于民主党人来说，在关键的 2028 年总统选举之前达成协议有真正的政治动机——特别是当该党寻求重新赢得选民对移民和边境安全的信任时，这些政策领域将在 2024 年给他们带来厄运。
“这些民主党人推翻了红色州，这也是为了他们的自身利益，对吧？不仅仅是为了说辞，做大事或者回家，而是实际上与总统、与共和党达成中间立场。因为如果不这样做，我认为这次选举的一个重要教训是，拉美裔选民将会逆转......如果他们看不到民主党在未来两年内做出任何贡献，”ABIC（ABIC）的执行董事丽贝卡·史（Rebecca Shi）说。支持移民改革的企业高管。
她补充说，如果共和党人不参加谈判，他们也能得到一个教训：“他们将失去白宫。”
白宫发言人劳伦·比斯赞扬了特朗普的移民成就，包括边境安全、犯罪率下降和国土安全特别工作组的成立，并表示总统“强有力的移民政策保持不变”。
她说，民主党人应该与特朗普合作，“确保我们南部边境的安全，将危险的非法罪犯从我们的社区中清除，并制止非法贩运致命毒品。”
民主党人对总统周日在《60 分钟》节目中的言论表示欢迎，当时他表示，他对一些没有犯罪、正在工作并为经济做出贡献的非法移民开放合法途径。穆林还对涉及 DACA 的两党移民改革持开放态度，该改革可能为一些儿童时期抵达美国的无证移民提供永久合法身份，尽管他和总统坚称任何提案都不包括特赦。

title_en: House Democrats prepare to elect leaders for the new Congress as party pushes for change
title_zh: 众议院民主党人准备选举新国会领导人，推动变革
summary: House Democrats are preparing to elect their leadership slate for the new Congress
summary_zh: 众议院民主党人正准备选举新一届国会的领导名单
body_en: House Democrats are preparing to elect their leadership slate for the new Congress
By LISA MASCARO AP congressional correspondent

WASHINGTON -- House Democrats are preparing to elect their leadership slate for the new Congress in closed-door meetings this week that will test Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries and the generation of new leaders who are running to take charge of their new majority.

Jeffries, with Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts, and Rep. Pete Aguilar of California, would all be historic firsts — as the first Black American to become House speaker, Clark as the first woman majority leader and Aguilar as the first Latino to serve as the majority whip. All three are running unopposed.

The trio of Democratic leaders faces a restive party eager for a fight after a change election , when voters ousted Republicans in a repudiation of President Donald Trump and the party in power. Phone calls and social media posts have been flooding the offices of Democrats and the newly-elected, demanding a fresh start. Protesters heckled Jeffries last week during a Democratic conference in Denver.

On Tuesday, Jeffries was meeting privately with the separate caucuses that make up the House Democrats — Congressional Progressive Caucus, the New Democrat Coalition and the fiscally conservative Blue Dogs, among others — ahead of the closed-door election. He has been personally reaching out to every House Democrat and says he is taking nothing for granted.
“I embrace those conversations, and we’re going to continue to do that over the next 24 hours,” he said.

Wednesday’s vote will be the first of their careers for dozens of members-elect , before they’re even sworn into office on Jan. 3, 2027, when the new Congress convenes. Jeffries, if reelected as Democratic leader, would face a separate roll call of the whole House in January to become speaker.

Rep.-elect Brad Lander of New York announced he would support Jeffries when he launched his campaign for Congress. Rep.-elect Randy Villegas of California has said he was supporting whoever would help him best deliver for his Central Valley district.

Returning Rep. Emily Randall, D-Wash., said she heard questions about House leadership during town halls in her district, and has been watching direct messages stream into her Instagram feed about the leadership election. So she decided to start dialing them back.
“People have messaged me asking if Bernie Sanders could be the speaker of the House,” she said. “Technically yes, and it would be probably difficult.”
(It's true that the House can elect anyone speaker, but also it's not likely to be Sanders since he already has a day job in the U.S. Senate.)

On one call, Randall said she listened to the constituent's concerns, and then told him, “Truthfully, not like blowing smoke, whoever is our speaker — and I think it is going to be Hakeem Jeffries, and I am supporting Hakeem Jeffries for speaker — I think we will accomplish a lot of the things that he was asking us to.”
Lawmakers pointed to the livestream that Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez did trying to explain the role of the speaker.

“There is one candidate in this race: Hakeem Jeffries,” Ocasio-Cortez said at the Capitol. “I think that everyone is far more concerned what that leadership means, what is it promising.”
Jeffries, Clark and Aguilar have risen together, as a team, as the first new generation of leaders of the post-Pelosi era, and soon their first time as leaders in the majority.
body_zh: 众议院民主党人正准备选举新一届国会的领导名单
美联社国会记者 LISA MASCARO
华盛顿——众议院民主党人正准备在本周的闭门会议上选举新一届国会的领导名单，这将考验民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯和即将竞选掌管新多数派的新一代领导人。
杰弗里斯与马萨诸塞州众议员凯瑟琳·克拉克（Katherine Clark）和加利福尼亚州众议员皮特·阿吉拉尔（Pete Aguilar）都将创造历史性的第一——成为第一位成为众议院议长的美国黑人，克拉克成为第一位女性多数党领袖，阿吉拉尔成为第一位担任多数党党鞭的拉丁裔。这三人都在无人反对的情况下奔跑。
这三位民主党领导人面临着一个焦躁不安的政党，他们在一场变革选举后渴望一场战斗，当时选民们因否认唐纳德·特朗普总统和执政党而驱逐了共和党人。民主党人和新当选者的办公室里充斥着电话和社交媒体帖子，要求重新开始。上周在丹佛举行的民主党会议上，抗议者质问杰弗里斯。
周二，在闭门选举之前，杰弗里斯与众议院民主党的各个核心小组进行了私下会面，其中包括国会进步党核心小组、新民主党联盟和财政保守的蓝狗党等。他亲自接触了每一位众议院民主党人，并表示他不会认为任何事情都是理所当然的。
“我欢迎这些对话，我们将在接下来的 24 小时内继续这样做，”他说。
周三的投票将是数十名当选议员职业生涯中的第一次投票，他们甚至在 2027 年 1 月 3 日新一届国会召开时宣誓就职。如果杰弗里斯再次当选民主党领袖，他将在一月份面临众议院全体议员的单独点名，以成为议长。
纽约当选众议员布拉德·兰德在杰弗里斯发起国会竞选活动时宣布他将支持杰弗里斯。加利福尼亚州当选众议员兰迪·维勒加斯 (Randy Villegas) 表示，他支持任何能帮助他最好地为中央谷区做出贡献的人。
华盛顿州民主党众议员艾米丽·兰德尔 (Emily Randall) 表示，她在所在选区的市政厅听到了有关众议院领导层的问题，并一直在关注她的 Instagram 上关于领导层选举的直接信息。所以她决定开始回拨他们。
“人们给我发信息询问伯尼·桑德斯是否可以担任众议院议长，”她说。 “从技术上讲是可以的，但这可能会很困难。”
（确实，众议院可以选举任何人为议长，但也不太可能是桑德斯，因为他已经在美国参议院有一份日常工作。）
兰德尔在一次电话会议上表示，她倾听了选民的担忧，然后告诉他，“说实话，无论谁是我们的发言人，都不像吹烟一样——我认为这将是哈基姆·杰弗里斯，我支持哈基姆·杰弗里斯担任发言人——我认为我们将完成他要求我们做的很多事情。”
议员们指出，众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯在直播中试图解释发言人的角色。
