“这场竞选中有一位候选人：哈基姆·杰弗里斯，”奥卡西奥-科尔特斯在国会大厦说。 “我认为每个人都更关心这种领导力意味着什么，它有什么前景。”
杰弗里斯、克拉克和阿吉拉尔作为一个团队一起崛起，成为后佩洛西时代的第一代新一代领导人，并且很快他们第一次成为多数派的领导人。

title_en: ICE agents pepper spray pregnant US citizen in California, video shows
title_zh: 视频显示，ICE特工在加州向怀孕的美国公民喷胡椒喷雾
summary: Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23, was arrested after being pushed to the ground and on to her stomach, her attorney says US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents pepper-sprayed a pregnant US citizen and threw her to the ground during a protest in Californ
summary_zh: 23 岁的莉兹贝丝·巴尔加斯·安德拉德 (Lizbeth Vargas Andrade) 的律师称，美国移民和海关执法局称她在被推倒在地并趴在地上后被捕。
body_en: Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23, was arrested after being pushed to the ground and on to her stomach, her attorney says

US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents pepper-sprayed a pregnant US citizen and threw her to the ground during a protest in California on Sunday, according to her family’s attorney, who shared footage of the incident.

Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23, was filming and protesting against the presence of several ICE officers outside the Stanislaus county jail in Modesto, in California’s Central valley, before she was taken down by officers and arrested while she was lying on her stomach during a chaotic encounter.

Vargas Andrade, who is 12 weeks pregnant, said in a press conference on Sunday evening that she was part of a group of local residents who monitor ICE sightings, and that she had gone to the jail parking lot after agents were spotted in the area.
A commotion erupted when ICE agents moved to arrest a man who, it appeared, had just been released from the jail, video shows.

Footage filmed by Vargas Andrade’s husband, Adolfo Talavera, captured a tumultuous scene as several people protested against the agents making the arrest. The circumstances of the man’s arrest were not immediately clear, and he has not been identified. Agents wore law enforcement vests and ICE badges, and at least two of them had masks covering their faces.

It was unclear what exactly happened right before Vargas Andrade’s arrest, with the sound on the footage repeatedly cutting out. One woman was heard screaming at the agents to get away from her and another cursed at the agents, telling them, “You should be embarrassed … you guys are so fucked up.”

Vargas Andrade had her phone in one hand as she and an agent then appeared to bump into each other, footage showed. That agent then grabbed her and started to handcuff her. Another agent then pulled out what appeared to be a pepper-spray canister and pointed it at the direction of Vargas Andrade and her husband who was filming.

The footage partially captured the agent deploying the pepper spray, though it was difficult to discern how long he sprayed it and where the chemicals landed. Soon after, the footage captured Talavera shouting, “She’s pregnant with child!” as the agents moved to detain his wife. Seconds later, two agents took Vargas Andrade to the ground where she was handcuffed on her stomach with her hands behind her back, before one of the agents moved her on to her side.

Vargas Andrade was taken into custody and transported to an ICE field office in Stockton, according to her attorney, Patrick Kolasinski. Vargas Andrade’s sister had called for an ambulance, which then arrived at the ICE facility and transported her to a hospital, her family and a local advocate said at the press conference.

Vargas Andrade said officers had told her she was accused of assaulting an ICE agent, an accusation she denied. She was released later that day, and she has not been charged with any crimes, according to Kolasinski.
Outcry after ICE violently detains US citizen walking to high school: ‘I thought they were going to kill me’

Spokespeople for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) did not respond to repeated inquiries on Monday, but said in a statement on Tuesday after publication that ICE agents had been arresting an undocumented man when a woman “actively interfered with, obstructed, and attempted to prevent the arrest – a federal crime”. The statement said an ICE officer “relied on his training to safely control the situation despite the combative, aggressive, and heinously vulgar conduct of the woman”.

A spokesperson for the Department of Justice declined to comment. A spokesperson for the Stanislaus sheriff’s office, which runs the jail, said sheriff deputies were not involved in Vargas Andrade’s arrest.

“They threw me to the ground, they maced me, then they handcuffed me,” Vargas Andrade recalled to reporters on Sunday night. “I told the ICE agent … ‘I’m pregnant, so don’t put your hands on me.’ … They right away threw me on the floor … I was burning. I couldn’t breathe. The mace went up my nose.”
Another ICE agent then gave her water to wash her face, she recalled.
“I got scared,” Talavera said. “I was like, what if she has a miscarriage?”
Vargas Andrade said she was particularly worried because she had suffered two previous pregnancy losses, but she said doctors did an ultrasound after the incident and did not identify any concerns.

The encounter happened amid reports of increased ICE activity in California’s Central valley region, which is home to the state’s agricultural industry. The DHS and the justice department have repeatedly accused anti-ICE protesters of assaulting agents, though many of those prosecutions in California have fallen apart in federal court .
body_zh: 23 岁的莉兹贝斯·巴尔加斯·安德拉德 (Lizbeth Vargas Andrade) 的律师称，她被推倒在地并趴在地上后被捕。
据她家人的律师分享了该事件的视频，据她家人的律师称，美国移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 人员周日在加利福尼亚州的一次抗议活动中向一名怀孕的美国公民喷了胡椒喷雾，并将她扔到地上。
23 岁的莉兹贝斯·巴尔加斯·安德拉德 (Lizbeth Vargas Andrade) 正在加利福尼亚州中央山谷莫德斯托的斯坦尼斯劳斯县监狱外拍摄并抗议几名 ICE 警察的出现，随后她在一次混乱的遭遇中趴着，被警察推倒并逮捕。
怀孕 12 周的巴尔加斯·安德拉德 (Vargas Andrade) 在周日晚上的新闻发布会上表示，她是监视 ICE 目击事件的当地居民小组的一员，在特工在该地区被发现后，她去了监狱停车场。
视频显示，当 ICE 特工逮捕一名似乎刚刚从监狱释放的男子时，引发了骚乱。
瓦尔加斯·安德拉德的丈夫阿道夫·塔拉维拉拍摄的视频捕捉到了混乱的场景，当时有几个人抗议特工的逮捕行动。目前尚不清楚该男子被捕的具体情况，其身份也尚未确定。特工身穿执法背心，佩戴 ICE 徽章，其中至少两人戴着口罩遮住脸部。
目前尚不清楚巴尔加斯·安德拉德被捕前究竟发生了什么，镜头中的声音不断被切断。一名女子向特工尖叫，要求他们远离她，另一名女子则咒骂特工，告诉他们，“你们应该感到尴尬……你们真是操蛋。”
录像显示，瓦尔加斯·安德拉德一手拿着手机，随后她和一名特工似乎撞到了对方。然后那个特工抓住了她并开始给她戴上手铐。另一名特工随后拿出一个似乎是胡椒喷雾罐的东西，并将其指向正在拍摄的瓦尔加斯·安德拉德和她丈夫的方向。
这段视频部分捕捉到了特工喷洒胡椒喷雾的画面，但很难辨别他喷洒了多长时间以及化学物质落在哪里。不久之后，镜头捕捉到塔拉维拉大喊：“她怀孕了！”当特工人员开始拘留他的妻子时。几秒钟后，两名特工将巴尔加斯·安德拉德（Vargas Andrade）按倒在地，双手背在背后，用手铐铐在腹部，然后其中一名特工将她移至一侧。
据她的律师帕特里克·科拉辛斯基 (Patrick Kolasinski) 称，瓦尔加斯·安德拉德 (Vargas Andrade) 已被拘留，并被送往 ICE 位于斯托克顿的办事处。她的家人和当地倡导者在新闻发布会上表示，瓦尔加斯·安德拉德的姐姐叫了一辆救护车，随后救护车抵达 ICE 设施并将她送往医院。
瓦尔加斯·安德拉德 (Vargas Andrade) 表示，警方告诉她，她被指控袭击 ICE 特工，但她否认了这一指控。科拉辛斯基说，她当天晚些时候被释放，没有被指控犯有任何罪行。
ICE 暴力拘留步行上高中的美国公民后引发强烈抗议：“我以为他们要杀了我”
美国国土安全部 (DHS) 发言人周一没有回应多次询问，但在周二发布的一份声明中表示，ICE 特工在逮捕一名无证男子时，一名女性“积极干扰、阻挠并试图阻止逮捕——这是一项联邦犯罪”。声明称，一名 ICE 官员“尽管这名女子表现出好斗、攻击性和令人发指的粗俗行为，但凭借他所受的训练安全地控制了局势”。
司法部发言人拒绝置评。管理该监狱的斯坦尼斯劳斯治安官办公室发言人表示，治安官代表没有参与逮捕巴尔加斯·安德拉德。
“他们把我扔到地上，用狼牙棒打我，然后给我戴上手铐，”瓦尔加斯·安德拉德周日晚上向记者回忆道。 “我告诉 ICE 特工……‘我怀孕了，所以不要把手放在我身上。’……他们立即把我扔到地板上……我浑身着火。我无法呼吸。狼牙棒进入了我的鼻子。”
她回忆说，另一名 ICE 特工随后给她水洗脸。
“我很害怕，”塔拉维拉说。 “我当时想，如果她流产了怎么办？”
瓦尔加斯·安德拉德说，她特别担心，因为她之前曾两次流产，但她说，医生在事件发生后做了超声波检查，没有发现任何问题。
此次遭遇事件发生之际，有报道称加州中央山谷地区的 ICE 活动有所增加，该地区是该州农业产业的所在地。国土安全部和司法部一再指控反 ICE 抗议者袭击特工，尽管加州的许多起诉在联邦法院都失败了。

title_en: US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991
title_zh: 由于1991年以来最严重的麻疹疫情，美国失去了消除麻疹的地位
summary: Infectious disease is now continually spreading after being eliminated for 26 years, with more than 5,400 US cases The US has lost its measles elimination status, global health authorities announced, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endem
summary_zh: 传染病在消除26年之后仍在持续蔓延，美国病例已超过5,400例 美国已经失去了消除麻疹的能力
body_en: Infectious disease is now continually spreading after being eliminated for 26 years, with more than 5,400 US cases
The US has lost its measles elimination status, global health authorities announced, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the US after being eliminated for 26 years.
The announcement comes as the US endures the worst measles outbreak since 1991, with more than 5,400 cases and eight deaths in 2026.

“Measles is resurging globally amid the persistent gaps in vaccination coverage, and this global trend is also affecting the Americas,” said Dr Jarbas Barbosa da Silva Jr, the director of the Pan American Health Organization, a regional branch of the World Health Organization . “The endemic measles transmission has now been re-established in Bolivia, Mexico and United States.” Silva made the final decision on US elimination status.

In a statement to the Guardian on Tuesday, Barbosa da Silva commended “the significant efforts undertaken by the United States to manage the measles outbreak through strengthened surveillance, timely case detection and response, targeted vaccination activities and coordination across the public health system”.

A global map of WHO measles elimination status. Much of the Asian and African continents have endemic status while South and Central America as well as Australia have verified elimination status. Canada and the US have re-established measles status.

Measles is one of the most contagious viruses known to medicine and requires 95% of the community to be vaccinated to prevent outbreaks. The measles vaccine is safe and highly effective. However, pockets of low vaccination have grown in the US following pandemic-era disruptions and widespread misinformation.
Measles, mumps and misinformation: how Crunchy Moms became ‘the most dangerous’ group on Facebook
The nation’s largest doctors group, the American Medical Association, described loss of measles elimination status as a “deeply troubling and entirely preventable setback for our nation”.

The loss of measles-free status comes after Donald Trump and his health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr , spent nearly two years sowing confusion about the safety of vaccines. In just one recent example, Trump called for the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) combination vaccine to be split into separate shots, arguing without evidence that “together, there could be a possibility they’re quite lethal”.

“As a pediatrician, I saw firsthand how decisions made in Washington hurt our children and families,” said Dr Annie Andrews, a Democratic senator-elect. “Nothing makes that clearer than the loss of our measles elimination status.” The loss of elimination status has already heightened criticism of Kennedy. High-profile epidemiologists called Kennedy’s work at the health department “malpractice” and equivalent to a “crime scene”.

In a statement posted on X late on Tuesday afternoon, Kennedy said the US “will stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain U.S. measles elimination status”. He added that he would “continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles” and that officials with the Department of Health & Human Services “are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust. We will answer families’ questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment.”
Barbosa da Silva called the role of misinformation in measles transmission “dynamic” and urged health departments to develop bespoke campaigns tailored to undervaccinated communities.

Experts caution against piling blame for measles outbreaks solely on the Trump administration . The MMR vaccine has been the target of misinformation for more than two decades, including work by Kennedy before his White House role.

“There is a profound problem with measles in all three North American countries,” said Noel Brewer, a behavioral scientist at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill who studies vaccination behaviors, and specifically measles. He chairs a committee that considers evidence on US measles elimination status, and contributed to the scientific work that underpinned Pan American Health Organization’s decision.
“The US has had large outbreaks and exported those to Canada and Mexico, and those cases have come back again to the US,” said Brewer.

Canada lost its measles-free status in 2025, but Barbosa da Silva said the country now represented the “good news” in the region. The nation stopped measles transmission for 60 days. This is the first step on the way to regaining measles elimination status. The UK and several European nations have also recently lost elimination status.

“What we’re experiencing is not a United States-specific thing,” said David Margolius of the Big Cities Health Coalition. Instead, there is a, “global surge in cases, global decline in vaccination rate”.
body_zh: 传染病在被消灭26年后，如今仍在持续蔓延，美国病例已超过5,400例
全球卫生当局宣布，美国已失去麻疹消除状态，正式承认这种传染病在消除麻疹26年后在美国流行。
这一消息发布之际，美国正在经历 1991 年以来最严重的麻疹疫情，到 2026 年将出现 5,400 多例病例和 8 人死亡。
世界卫生组织地区分支机构泛美卫生组织主任贾巴斯·巴博萨·达席尔瓦博士表示：“由于疫苗接种覆盖率持续存在差距，麻疹在全球范围内卷土重来，这一全球趋势也正在影响美洲。” “麻疹地方性传播现已在玻利维亚、墨西哥和美国重新出现。”席尔瓦对美国队的淘汰状态做出了最终决定。
巴尔博萨·达席尔瓦在周二向《卫报》发表的一份声明中赞扬“美国通过加强监测、及时发现和应对病例、有针对性的疫苗接种活动以及整个公共卫生系统的协调，为控制麻疹疫情所做的重大努力”。
世界卫生组织麻疹消除状况的全球地图。亚洲和非洲大陆的大部分地区都处于流行状态，而南美洲和中美洲以及澳大利亚已证实已消除。加拿大和美国重新确立了麻疹地位。
麻疹是医学上已知的最具传染性的病毒之一，需要社区 95% 的人接种疫苗才能预防疫情爆发。麻疹疫苗安全且高效。然而，由于大流行时代的破坏和广泛的错误信息，美国的疫苗接种率较低的情况有所增加。
麻疹、腮腺炎和错误信息：Crunchy Moms 如何成为 Facebook 上“最危险”的群体
美国最大的医生团体美国医学会将麻疹消除地位的丧失描述为“对我们国家来说是一个令人深感不安且完全可以预防的挫折”。
在唐纳德·特朗普和他的卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪花了近两年的时间对疫苗的安全性造成混乱之后，美国失去了无麻疹状态。仅在最近的一个例子中，特朗普就呼吁将麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 联合疫苗分成单独的疫苗，并在没有证据的情况下辩称，“三者合用，可能具有相当致命性”。
“作为一名儿科医生，我亲眼目睹了华盛顿做出的决定如何伤害我们的孩子和家庭，”当选民主党参议员安妮·安德鲁斯博士说。 “没有什么比麻疹消除状态的丧失更能说明这一点了。”失去淘汰地位已经加剧了对肯尼迪的批评。备受瞩目的流行病学家称肯尼迪在卫生部门的工作是“渎职”，相当于“犯罪现场”。
肯尼迪在周二下午晚些时候在 X 上发布的一份声明中表示，美国“将阻止麻疹疫情，保护美国家庭，并努力恢复美国麻疹消除状态”。他补充说，他将“继续推荐 MMR 疫苗接种作为预防麻疹的最有效方法”，卫生与公众服务部的官员“正在努力缩小疫苗接种差距并重建公众信任。我们将诚实地回答家庭有关疫苗益处和风险的问题，并与值得信赖的医疗保健提供者和社区领袖合作，预防麻疹、限制其传播并支持及时治疗。”
巴博萨·达席尔瓦称错误信息在麻疹传播中的作用是“动态的”，并敦促卫生部门针对疫苗接种不足的社区开展定制活动。
专家警告不要将麻疹疫情的爆发完全归咎于特朗普政府。二十多年来，MMR 疫苗一直是错误信息的目标，包括肯尼迪在担任白宫职务之前的工作。
“这三个北美国家都存在严重的麻疹问题，”北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校的行为科学家诺埃尔·布鲁尔（Noel Brewer）说，他研究疫苗接种行为，特别是麻疹。他担任一个委员会的主席，负责审议有关美国麻疹消除状况的证据，并为支持泛美卫生组织决定的科学工作做出了贡献。
布鲁尔说：“美国爆发了大规模疫情，并将其输出到加拿大和墨西哥，而这些病例又回到了美国。”
加拿大于 2025 年失去了无麻疹状态，但巴博萨·达席尔瓦表示，该国现在代表了该地区的“好消息”。该国已阻止麻疹传播 60 天。这是恢复消除麻疹状态的第一步。英国和几个欧洲国家最近也失去了淘汰地位。
“我们所经历的并不是美国特有的事情，”大城市健康联盟的大卫·马戈利乌斯说。相反，“全球病例激增，全球疫苗接种率下降”。

title_en: Democrats with 2028 ambitions say their party still must prove itself to win the White House: From the Politics Desk
title_zh: 拥有 2028 年雄心的民主党人表示，他们的政党仍必须证明自己才能赢得白宫：来自政治部门
summary: In today’s edition, Natasha Korecki files a dispatch from a recent gathering of jubilant, but forward-looking, Democrats in Denver.
summary_zh: 在今天的版本中，娜塔莎·科雷茨基 (Natasha Korecki) 提交了最近在丹佛举行的一次欢欣鼓舞但具有前瞻性的民主党人聚会的快讯。
body_en: Shapiro 2028? Pennsylvania Gov. says he’s focused on the commonwealth ‘right now’

In today’s edition, Natasha Korecki files a dispatch from a recent gathering of jubilant, but forward-looking, Democrats in Denver. Plus, Peter Nicholas and Jared Perlo dig into President Donald Trump’s relationship with former (and possibly future?) Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Democrats with 2028 ambitions say their party still must prove itself to win the White House
DENVER — They came to celebrate, to gloat and to reflect. But mostly, they came to launch the next chapter.
The convening of some 3,500 Democrats at the “What’s Next” conference organized by Majority Democrats here last week made a couple of things clear.

First is the most obvious: While the party was still riding high after the midterms, it couldn’t wait to move into a 2028 presidential posture. Governors, members of Congress and former Cabinet secretaries took turns testing messages onstage and taking a spin before reporters.

The second thing may be refreshing news to their party: Democrats across the board seemed to understand that they can’t rest on their laurels and need to use their newly won power to come through in a big way and quickly. Otherwise, in two years they’ll be out again.
Speaker after speaker conveyed that the shifts that swept them into office were temporary. They realize that Americans dislike both parties, they just dislike Republicans more right now.

Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro , who is exploring a White House run, said that to sustain trust into 2028, Democrats had to reverse President Donald Trump’s unpopular policies by ending tariffs and blocking Iran war funding.

“We all have to marshal every tool we have that the people just put in our hands,” Shapiro said. “That means ending this reckless war and these tariffs that drive up our prices and drive away our allies. Bringing accountability to the sweetheart deals, the mass agents, the use of American weapons on open seas and across the globe.”
Meanwhile, Democrats like Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan and Sen.-elect James Talarico of Texas said that they would work with Trump if it meant getting a key policy priority over the goal line.

“Our job as elected leaders is to deliver real things for people, so if slapping Trump’s name on it and putting it in gold letters would get it through, hell yes, I would do that,” Slotkin said. “I’m going to be measured and graded on what actually happens for people in Michigan.”
Of a possible 2028 bid, Slotkin said, “I am looking at it seriously.”
Other Democratic presidential contenders, including Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona, Sen. Cory Booker of New Jersey and Rep. Ro Khanna of California, were also part of the fray in Denver.

For his part, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg urged his party to work with speed once they took control of Congress in January. “I am hopeful that instead of getting gummed up in a 1,000-page bill that takes six months to put together, we come out of the gate with a rapid fire of things that will put money back in people’s pockets,” Buttigieg told reporters.
And Sen. Raphael Warnock of Georgia said that if Americans were to believe that Democrats were fighting for them, they had to put money into their pockets.

“Only a nation that is spiritually broken, only a people that were already deeply disappointed could have elected the likes of Donald Trump twice,” Warnock said. “And so this fight is a moral fight. We must raise worker wages and the index of our moral imagination. We must heal the land. And we can.”
Hakeem Jeffries endorses lowering Medicare age, adding benefits and universal coverage for kids , by Sahil Kapur
Democrats weigh how far to go with their newfound power in the states , by Adam Edelman
body_zh: 夏皮罗 2028？宾夕法尼亚州州长表示他“现在”专注于英联邦
在今天的版本中，娜塔莎·科雷茨基 (Natasha Korecki) 提交了最近在丹佛举行的一次欢欣鼓舞但具有前瞻性的民主党人聚会的快讯。此外，彼得·尼古拉斯 (Peter Nicholas) 和贾里德·佩洛 (Jared Perlo) 深入探讨了唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 总统与前（也可能是未来？） Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的关系。
拥有 2028 年雄心的民主党人表示，他们的政党仍必须证明自己才能入主白宫
丹佛——他们来这里是为了庆祝、幸灾乐祸和反思。但最重要的是，他们来开启下一个篇章。
上周，约 3,500 名民主党人参加了由民主党多数派组织的“下一步是什么”会议，这清楚地表明了一些事情。
首先是最明显的：虽然该党在中期选举后仍处于高位，但它迫不及待地想进入 2028 年总统大选。州长、国会议员和前内阁部长轮流在台上测试信息并在记者面前进行演示。
第二件事可能对他们的政党来说是令人耳目一新的消息：全体民主党人似乎都明白，他们不能满足于现状，需要利用他们新赢得的权力来快速、大规模地实现目标。不然两年后他们就会再次出局。
一个又一个的发言者都表示，让他们上任的转变是暂时的。他们意识到美国人不喜欢两党，他们只是现在更不喜欢共和党。
正在考虑竞选白宫的宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗 (Josh Shapiro) 表示，为了将信任维持到 2028 年，民主党必须通过终止关税和阻止伊朗战争资金来扭转唐纳德·特朗普总统不受欢迎的政策。
夏皮罗说：“我们所有人都必须整理人们刚刚交给我们的所有工具。” “这意味着结束这场鲁莽的战争和这些抬高我们的价格并赶走我们的盟友的关税。对甜心交易、大规模特工、在公海和全球范围内使用美国武器进行问责。”
与此同时，密歇根州参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金(Elissa Slotkin)和德克萨斯州当选参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科(James Talarico)等民主党人表示，如果这意味着获得超越目标线的关键政策优先事项，他们将与特朗普合作。
斯洛特金说：“作为民选领导人，我们的工作是为人民提供实实在在的东西，所以如果把特朗普的名字印在上面并用金字写上就能成功，我会这么做的，是的，我会这么做。” “我将根据密歇根州人们的实际情况进行衡量和评分。”
对于 2028 年可能的申办，斯洛特金表示，“我正在认真考虑。”
其他民主党总统候选人，包括亚利桑那州参议员鲁本·加莱戈、新泽西州参议员科里·布克和加利福尼亚州众议员罗·卡纳，也参与了丹佛的角逐。
前交通部长皮特·布蒂吉格则敦促他的政党在一月份控制国会后迅速开展工作。布蒂吉格对记者表示：“我希望，我们不会陷入一份需要六个月才能完成的 1000 页法案，而是迅速推出一系列能让人们把钱重新带回口袋的法案。”
佐治亚州参议员拉斐尔·沃诺克表示，如果美国人相信民主党正在为他们而战，他们就必须把钱放进自己的口袋。
沃诺克说：“只有一个精神上破碎的国家，只有一个已经深感失望的人民才能两次当选唐纳德·特朗普这样的人。” “所以这场斗争是一场道德斗争。我们必须提高工人工资和道德想象力指数。我们必须治愈这片土地。我们可以。”
哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 支持降低医疗保险年龄、增加儿童福利和全民覆盖，作者：Sahil Kapur

title_en: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody
title_zh: 八岁海地男孩从 ICE 拘留释放后返回家中
summary: Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility i
summary_zh: 在圣地亚哥被移民人员拘留并转移到德克萨斯州后与家人团聚的八岁海地男孩
body_en: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement)
Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas

An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California .

Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas . Today, he’s finally home.”
The Haitian Bridge Alliance, an immigration advocacy group, confirmed that the third-grader had been released from Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) custody.

“An eight-year-old child belongs in a classroom, on a playground, and surrounded by love – not in immigration detention. We welcome his release, but his freedom should never have required a public outcry,” Guerline Jozef, executive director of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, said in a statement.
Hundreds protest against ex-border patrol chief Greg Bovino at Rutgers University talk

The third-grader at Fay elementary school was put in restraints and taken into custody by federal immigration officers at a check-in earlier in the month, according to video obtained by NBC News and an oversight letter Democratic lawmakers sent to the Departments of Homeland Security and Health and Human Services.
A spokesperson for the homeland security department said ICE took the child into custody “out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child’s safety”.

The uncle, the spokesperson said in a statement to the Guardian, was unable to prove legal guardianship – and that officials were obliged by federal anti-trafficking laws to take the boy into care as an “unaccompanied alien child”.
The Haitian Bridge Alliance said the boy was in the care of his uncle and cousins after his father was deported last year.

“I’m so grateful that he’s home, but this should have never happened in the first place,” Vargas said in a second social media post, adding that he would be asking the Trump administration for answers. While he was detained, the child was “held in a facility in Texas, far away from his home in San Diego”, Vargas said.

Celebrating the boy’s return, Jozef of the Haitian Bridge Alliance told NBC News : “The aunt was literally crying, and she said: ‘I have not eaten since the Wednesday they took my baby.’ They haven’t been able to sleep because of that.” She added: “The cousins were there when they took him, and wondering: will they ever see him again? But today [Monday] they are able to see him again. They are able to hug him.”
body_zh: 八岁海地男孩从 ICE 拘留释放后返回家中ICE（美国移民和海关执法局）
孩子在圣地亚哥被移民官员拘留并转移到德克萨斯州后与家人团聚
一名 8 岁海地男孩于 11 月 4 日在圣地亚哥被移民人员束缚并拘留，并被转移到德克萨斯州的一处设施，现已与加利福尼亚州的家人团聚。
众议员胡安·巴尔加斯（Juan Vargas）在 Monda 的社交媒体帖子中分享了男孩和他家人的照片，并写道：“11 天前，圣地亚哥一名 8 岁的孩子在移民登记时被联邦拘留。他与亲人失散，被关押在德克萨斯州的一处设施中。今天，他终于回家了。”
移民倡导组织海地桥梁联盟证实，这名三年级学生已被移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 释放。
“一个八岁的孩子应该在教室里，在操场上，被爱​​包围，而不是在移民拘留所里。我们欢迎他的释放，但他的自由不应该需要公众的强烈抗议，”海地桥梁联盟执行董事居尔兰·约瑟夫在一份声明中说。
数百人在罗格斯大学演讲中抗议前边境巡逻队长格雷格·博维诺
根据NBC新闻获得的视频以及民主党议员发给国土安全部和卫生与公众服务部的监督信，本月早些时候，联邦移民官员在检查时对费伊小学三年级学生进行了限制和拘留。
国土安全部发言人表示，ICE 拘留孩子是“出于高度谨慎并确保孩子的安全”。
发言人在给《卫报》的一份声明中表示，这名叔叔无法证明其合法监护权，并且根据联邦反人口贩卖法，官员们有义务将这名男孩作为“无人陪伴的外国儿童”予以照顾。
海地桥梁联盟表示，男孩的父亲去年被驱逐出境后，由他的叔叔和表兄弟照顾。
瓦尔加斯在第二条社交媒体帖子中表示：“我很感激他能回家，但这本来就不应该发生。”他补充说，他将向特朗普政府寻求答案。瓦尔加斯说，在他被拘留期间，孩子“被关押在德克萨斯州的一个设施中，远离他在圣地亚哥的家”。
海地桥梁联盟的约瑟夫在庆祝男孩回归时告诉美国全国广播公司新闻：“阿姨真的哭了，她说：‘自从他们带走我的孩子的那个星期三以来，我就没吃过东西。’因此他们无法入睡。”她补充道：“当他们带走他时，堂兄弟们就在那里，他们想知道：他们还能再见到他吗？但今天（周一）他们能够再次见到他。他们能够拥抱他。”

title_en: Markwayne Mullin defends private-jet trip to football game as millions hit by flight delays
title_zh: 马克韦恩·穆林 (Markwayne Mullin) 为私人飞机前往足球比赛辩护，因为数百万人因航班延误而受到影响
summary: Trump homeland security chief says ‘we still got to live our life’ amid outcry over journey to LSU on government plane The US homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, has defended his decision to fly in a private government jet to a college football game
summary_zh: 特朗普国土安全负责人表示，在乘坐政府飞机前往路易斯安那州立大学的强烈抗议中，“我们仍然要过我们的生活” 美国国土安全秘密
body_en: Markwayne Mullin defends private-jet trip to football game as millions hit by flight delays | Trump administration
Trump homeland security chief says ‘we still got to live our life’ amid outcry over journey to LSU on government plane

The US homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, has defended his decision to fly in a private government jet to a college football game on Saturday as Americans weathered widespread flight delays and cancellations , saying: “We still got to live our life.”

Mullin, a former US senator from Oklahoma, traveled on a government aircraft on Saturday to watch a football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas, the New York Post reported on Tuesday . The trip to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, came about a day after a four-hour ground stop that led to thousands of flights being delayed or cancelled – and an estimated 1.5 million people were stranded.
Evidently, botched maintenance work upgrading telecommunication lines from old copper wire to fiber optic cables in at least one remote location prompted the FAA to implement the ground stop.

Mullin is required to travel on a government aircraft with secure communication systems and pay back the government for personal travel. Still, the homeland security secretary defended his decision to travel for pleasure while many other Americans were stranded.
“We would have never went if the airlines – if the airways – weren’t completely open. [And] they’d been completely open for 21 hours,” Mullin said in an interview on CNBC on Tuesday.
“I would have never taken airspace if the airspace wasn’t open and we still got to live our life at the same time.
“We still have family, friends, and we also have work we do every day.”

Mullin spent part of the game in the box of Ben Bordelon, CEO of Bollinger Shipping, a company that has Department of Homeland Security contracts, the Post reported. Mullin said on CNBC he did not know Bordelon.

He defended his travel as Republicans have sought to shift blame away from Donald Trump’s administration for the nationwide ground stop to Congress and the Joe Biden White House before Trump’s second presidency.
Democrats have said that characterization is “absurd”, noting that both the Biden administration and Congress have allocated tens of billions of dollars for air traffic control improvements.
body_zh: 马克韦恩·穆林 (Markwayne Mullin) 为数百万人因航班延误而乘坐私人飞机观看足球比赛进行辩护特朗普政府
特朗普国土安全部部长表示，在乘坐政府飞机前往路易斯安那州立大学的强烈抗议中，“我们仍然要过我们的生活”
美国国土安全部长马克韦恩·穆林（Markwayne Mullin）为自己周六乘坐政府私人飞机观看大学橄榄球比赛的决定进行了辩护，他说：“我们仍然要过我们的生活。”
据《纽约邮报》周二报道，来自俄克拉荷马州的前美国参议员穆林周六乘坐政府飞机观看了路易斯安那州立大学和德克萨斯大学之间的橄榄球比赛。飞往路易斯安那州巴吞鲁日的航班大约在一天前经历了四个小时的地面停留，导致数千架航班延误或取消，估计有 150 万人被困。
显然，至少在一个偏远地区，将电信线路从旧铜线升级为光缆的维护工作失败，促使美国联邦航空管理局实施了地面停飞。
穆林被要求乘坐具有安全通信系统的政府飞机出行，并向政府偿还个人旅行费用。尽管如此，国土安全部长还是为自己在许多其他美国人陷入困境时出游的决定进行了辩护。
“如果航空公司——如果航空公司——没有完全开放，我们永远不会去。[而且]他们已经完全开放了 21 个小时，”穆林周二在接受 CNBC 采访时表示。
“如果空域不开放，我就永远不会进入空域，而且我们仍然要同时过自己的生活。
“我们还有家人、朋友，我们也有每天要做的工作。”
据《华盛顿邮报》报道，穆林在博林格航运公司首席执行官本·博德隆的包厢里度过了部分比赛，该公司与国土安全部有合同。穆林在 CNBC 上表示，他不认识博德隆。
他为自己的旅行进行了辩护，因为共和党人试图将特朗普政府在全国范围内停留的责任转移到国会和乔·拜登在特朗普担任第二任总统之前的白宫。
民主党人表示，这种描述是“荒谬的”，并指出拜登政府和国会都已拨款数百亿美元用于改善空中交通管制。

title_en: National Security Agency network for internal communications goes down
title_zh: 国家安全局内部通信网络瘫痪
summary: NSA issues ‘code yellow’ as NSANet, used by staff to share classified material, including top-secret intelligence, fails The US National Security Agency said on Tuesday that it had experienced “temporary degradation” during scheduled routine maintenance, after
summary_zh: 美国国家安全局发布“黄色代码”，因为员工使用 NSANet 共享机密材料（包括绝密情报）失败
body_en: NSA issues ‘code yellow’ as NSANet, used by staff to share classified material, including top-secret intelligence, fails

The US National Security Agency said on Tuesday that it had experienced “temporary degradation” during scheduled routine maintenance, after reports that its classified internal communications network had gone down.

In a statement, the agency said some internal systems were affected but that “mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational” and its ability to defend national security continues. It said its infrastructure is built with “multiple layers of redundancy” to keep operations running during planned maintenance or unexpected events.
The statement did not name the network, say what caused the problem or how long it lasted, or say whether service had been fully restored.
Gmail and Apple’s apps suffer outages days after major Microsoft disruptions

The New York Times and CNN had earlier reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that NSANet, the network the agency uses to send and receive classified information including top-secret material, was offline on Tuesday. They said staff at the agency’s Fort Meade, Maryland, headquarters had been told to stagger their arrivals while it assessed the problem. The Wall Street Journal also reported the outage, citing one person familiar with the situation, who said it stemmed from a software update to patch the system and that it would only be down temporarily.

The Times reported that a recorded message on an employee information line described a “code yellow”, the second-highest level in a three-tier alert system, for the day shift. Non-emergency staff were told not to come in before noon, while emergency personnel were to report as scheduled, the paper said.

Both CNN and the Times, citing people familiar with the matter, said there was no sign so far that the outage was caused by a cyber-attack or other malicious activity. The Times, citing one person, reported that the network had been unstable for weeks, and had been a cause of frustration among staff.

A former senior NSA cybersecurity official, who has no knowledge of the incident beyond public reports, speculated that several software patches may have been applied at once and something had gone wrong.

The outage follows a run of technology failures in the US in recent days, including a nationwide ground stop of flights , a Microsoft outage and disruption to banking services . None of those have been tied to a cyber-attack, though the causes of some have not been fully explained. Officials said the ground stop was not the result of malicious activity by a foreign actor, and the transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, said they were investigating whether contractor error or a faulty router was responsible.
Trump has not commented directly on the NSA outage. Asked in Manila on Tuesday about the constant outages, he played them down, saying such problems were inevitable: “Things like that happen.”
Microsoft identifies months-old bug as a root cause of global outage
He said he had spoken with banks and that the situation would be “very much under control”, and that Americans travelling before Thanksgiving were safe.

Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, called for the Trump administration to send officials to brief lawmakers on Capitol Hill about the recent nationwide technical and infrastructure outages, telling reporters that the public deserves more transparency around the widespread disruptions.

While none of the incidents have been classified as a cyber-attack, Mike Wiacek, a former US Department of Defense analyst, said the run of failures in a single week was a reason for caution and that early assurances may have come too quickly.

“Without data, I can’t say for certain whether this is or isn’t a cyber-attack,” Wiacek said. “But four major outages in under a week ( Outlook , the FAA , the banks and now the NSA) look suspiciously like what I’d expect one to look like.
“What concerns me most is how quickly officials ruled out an attack,” he said. “You can’t compress months of forensic work into a few hours.”
body_zh: 美国国家安全局发布“黄色代码”，因为工作人员用来共享机密材料（包括绝密情报）的 NSANet 失败
美国国家安全局周二表示，在有报道称其机密内部通信网络出现故障后，该局在定期例行维护期间经历了“暂时性能下降”。
该机构在一份声明中表示，一些内部系统受到了影响，但“关键任务能力仍然全面运行”，并且其捍卫国家安全的能力仍在继续。该公司表示，其基础设施采用“多层冗余”构建，以在计划维护或意外事件期间保持运营正常运行。
声明没有透露该网络的名称，也没有说明问题的原因或问题持续了多长时间，也没有说明服务是否已完全恢复。
微软重大中断几天后，Gmail 和苹果应用程序遭遇中断
《纽约时报》和 CNN 早些时候援引知情人士的话报道称，该机构用来发送和接收包括绝密材料在内的机密信息的网络 NSANet 于周二离线。他们表示，该机构马里兰州米德堡总部的工作人员已被告知在评估问题时错开抵达时间。 《华尔街日报》也报道了此次故障，并援引一位知情人士的话称，故障源于修补系统的软件更新，并且只会暂时停机。
《纽约时报》报道称，员工信息热线上的一条录音信息描述了白班的“黄色代码”，这是三级警报系统中的第二高级别。该报称，非急救人员被告知不要在中午之前进来，而急救人员则应按计划报到。
美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 和《泰晤士报》均援引知情人士的话称，到目前为止，没有迹象表明此次中断是由网络攻击或其他恶意活动造成的。 《泰晤士报》援引一位知情人士的话报道称，该网络已经不稳定了数周，导致员工感到沮丧。
一名美国国家安全局前高级网络安全官员除了公开报道外对这一事件一无所知，他推测可能是同时应用了多个软件补丁，导致出现了问题。
这次中断是在美国最近几天发生一系列技术故障之后发生的，其中包括全国范围内的航班停飞、微软宕机以及银行服务中断。尽管其中一些事件的原因尚未得到充分解释，但这些事件都与网络攻击无关。官员们表示，这次地面停车并不是外国行为者恶意活动的结果，交通部长肖恩·达菲表示，他们正在调查到底是承包商失误还是路由器故障造成的。
特朗普尚未直接对美国国家安全局的停电事件发表评论。周二在马尼拉被问及持续停电的情况时，他淡化了这些问题，称此类问题是不可避免的：“这样的事情时有发生。”
微软将几个月前的错误确定为全球服务中断的根本原因
他表示，他已经与银行进行了交谈，情况将“在很大程度上得到控制”，感恩节前旅行的美国人是安全的。
众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 呼吁特朗普政府派官员向国会山的立法者通报最近全国范围内的技术和基础设施中断情况，并告诉记者，公众应该对广泛的中断有更多的透明度。
虽然这些事件都没有被归类为网络攻击，但前美国国防部分析师迈克·威亚塞克 (Mike Wiacek) 表示，一周内发生的一系列故障需要保持谨慎，而且早期的保证可能来得太快了。
“没有数据，我无法确定这是否是网络攻击，”维亚切克说。 “但一周内发生的四次重大停电（Outlook、FAA、银行和现在的 NSA）看起来与我预期的情况令人怀疑。
“我最担心的是官员们多快就排除了袭击，”他说。 “你无法将几个月的取证工作压缩为几个小时。”

title_en: Nvidia board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
title_zh: 英伟达董事会表示不打算恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官
summary: The former Nvidia CEO said he would be "honored" to return if the board allowed. But the board says it has no intention of reinstating him.
summary_zh: 这位前英伟达首席执行官表示，如果董事会允许，他将“很荣幸”回归。但董事会表示无意恢复他的职位。
body_en: Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO : NPR
Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO The former Nvidia CEO said he would be "honored" to return if the board allowed. But the board says it has no intention of reinstating him.

A pedestrian walks in front of a Nvidia sign outside the company's headquarters on Nov. 12, 2026 in Santa Clara, Calif. after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO. Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images hide caption
Nvidia said it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, amid a push by the former CEO's allies to return him to lead the chipmaker he cofounded.

Huang "voluntarily resigned" on Nov. 12 after disclosing "personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms," board chair Harvey Jones said on the company's earnings call on Tuesday afternoon. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang had said he would return to lead the company he cofounded if Nvidia's board allowed him to. Huang also agreed to appear before Congress to answer questions about the national security scandals swirling around the company.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang wrote in a statement posted on social media . "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation."
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal

Huang stepped down from the company last week after acknowledging that he had been unfaithful to his wife. News reports have tied him to a woman who U.S. intelligence officials say was recruited by China's spy agency , as well as with another woman who is an executive at Nvidia. NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.

Huang said he would be "honored" to return to the company if Nvidia's board agreed. His comments came as some in Silicon Valley have tried to argue that Huang was pushed out of the company too quickly, and circulated a petition to "stand with Jensen."

"We don't want rushes to judgment. We don't want political pressure from the left or the right to force a board into action before we've even taken the time to turn over the cards and learn what was done," said Brad Gerstner, the founder and CEO of Altimeter Capital, an investor in Nvidia, at Semafor's Silicon Valley and the World conference on Monday.

Huang and Nvidia's general counsel Tim Teter will answer questions behind closed doors from the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committees and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party on Dec. 1st and 2nd.

Lawmakers say they want answers about Nvidia's role in alleged chip smuggling and efforts to evade export controls meant to block China from accessing the most advanced U.S. AI chips. They will also ask Huang about his involvement with Alice Huang , who was an executive with Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company that was a major customer for Nvidia's chips. In a statement emailed to NPR, Megaspeed said it "conducts legitimate and lawful business," and that Alice Huang left the company in 2025, but that it is conducting an internal investigation.
Nvidia's board said on Tuesday it had formed a committee to oversee the company's national security policies, compliance with U.S. export controls, and risk management of global trade.
U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout

On Monday, the U.S. Commerce Department announced new rules to prevent remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers, closing a loophole that may have let Chinese companies remotely access advanced Nvidia chips through overseas data centers. The Commerce Department and Justice Department also announced Monday that the DOJ is conducting a criminal investigation of Megaspeed.
Nvidia sought to reassure investors about the company's future during its third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday.

"Our ambition will not change. Our passion to innovate will not change. And our commitment to customers, partners and shareholders will not change," said Colette Kress, the company's chief financial officer who is serving as interim CEO while the board finds a permanent leader.
Quarterly sales doubled to a record $115.8 billion and profit also doubled to $65.3 billion from a year ago. The company said it was raising its forecast for sales growth next year.

董事会主席 Harvey Jones 在周二下午的公司财报电话会议上表示，黄在披露“个人行为不符合公司行为准则、标准和文化规范”后，于 11 月 12 日“主动辞职”。 “英伟达董事会一致接受他的辞职，并且不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官。”
周二早些时候，黄仁勋曾表示，如果英伟达董事会允许，他将重返领导他共同创立的公司。黄还同意出席国会，回答有关该公司的国家安全丑闻的问题。
黄仁勋在社交媒体上发布的一份声明中写道：“我没有达到 NVIDIA 每个人的期望标准，而且我在个人生活中犯了严重错误。我给董事会带来了问题，对此我深感遗憾。” “我完全承认自己的错误，并且我致力于配合董事会的独立调查。”
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因涉嫌间谍丑闻辞职
黄上周在承认自己对妻子不忠后辞去了公司职务。新闻报道称他与一名美国情报官员称其为中国间谍机构招募的女性以及另一名英伟达高管女性有联系。 NPR 尚未独立证实这些报道。
黄仁勋表示，如果英伟达董事会同意，他将“很荣幸”重返公司。在他发表上述言论之际，硅谷的一些人试图辩称黄被太快地赶出了公司，并散发了一份“与詹森站在一起”的请愿书。
英伟达投资者 Altimeter Capital 的创始人兼首席执行官 Brad Gerstner 周一在 Semafor 的硅谷和世界会议上表示：“我们不希望仓促做出判断。我们不希望在我们花时间翻牌并了解所做的事情之前，来自左派或右派的政治压力迫使董事会采取行动。”
黄仁勋和英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特将于 12 月 1 日至 2 日在众议院外交事务和情报委员会以及众议院中国共产党特别委员会闭门回答问题。

立法者表示，他们希望了解英伟达在涉嫌芯片走私以及逃避旨在阻止中国获得最先进的美国人工智能芯片的出口管制方面所扮演的角色的答案。他们还将询问黄与 Alice Huang 的关系，Alice Huang 是一家总部位于新加坡的公司 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司是 Nvidia 芯片的主要客户。在通过电子邮件发送给 NPR 的声明中，Megaspeed 表示其“开展合法且合法的业务”，Alice Huang 于 2025 年离开该公司，但正在进行内部调查。
英伟达董事会周二表示，已成立一个委员会来监督该公司的国家安全政策、美国出口管制的遵守情况以及全球贸易的风险管理。
由于英伟达的影响，美国加强了对远程访问人工智能技术的控制
周一，美国商务部宣布了新规则，禁止远程访问先进的人工智能芯片和服务器，堵住了可能让中国企业通过海外数据中心远程访问先进的英伟达芯片的漏洞。美国商务部和司法部周一还宣布，司法部正在对 Megaspeed 进行刑事调查。
英伟达在周二的第三季度财报电话会议上试图向投资者保证公司的未来。
该公司首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 表示：“我们的雄心不会改变。我们对创新的热情不会改变。我们对客户、合作伙伴和股东的承诺也不会改变。”
与去年同期相比，季度销售额翻了一番，达到创纪录的 1158 亿美元，利润也翻了一番，达到了 653 亿美元。该公司表示，将提高明年的销售增长预期。

title_en: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
title_zh: 加州因黑客风险起诉 OpenAI
summary: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

body_en: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced a lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday Nov. 16, 2026. In the complaint, California alleged that OpenAI misled the public about how unsafe its products are. California Department of Justice/Screenshot by NPR hide caption
California Department of Justice/Screenshot by NPR

California sued OpenAI Monday, alleging that the frontier AI company failed to protect the public from its systems' advanced cyber capabilities. The lawsuit stems from OpenAI's agents' attack on open-source software platform Hugging Face over the summer but also touches on a wide range of other related incidents tied to the company's agents acting without authorization.

"Just because the technology is new or rapidly evolving doesn't mean the people behind it are above the law," said California Attorney General Rob Bonta during a press conference. "Whether it's a car or a toy, the law is simple: don't build or test things that can hurt people without proper safeguards." The lawsuit cited potential concerns about cyberattacks "on power grids, emergency infrastructure, hospital systems, and financial institutions."
Why did OpenAI's and Anthropic's AI models hack other companies?

In the complaint , California alleged that OpenAI misled the public about how unsafe its products are. The state said the company admitted to the attorney general's office that "it lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing."

That number is higher than what OpenAI has so far disclosed publicly and more than what outside researchers have independently discovered, but OpenAI has otherwise provided little information, California said. The state also accused OpenAI of poor security practices, stonewalling the state's investigation into the company and discouraging employees from speaking up about safety.

In a statement to NPR, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab" and that the company has "engaged—and will continue to engage—constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry."
Fired OpenAI employees question the company's commitment to safety

After the most notorious of cyber incidents involving OpenAI's agents – the attack on Hugging Face over the summer – the company admitted that it did not monitor its agents in ways its own researchers deemed important. Since then, outside researchers as well as OpenAI itself have found more incidents in which AI agents have interacted with websites and communicated with each other on the internet in ways that OpenAI did not intend. The lawsuit mentions these events as well as other incidents that OpenAI started disclosing voluntarily to the public.

Other AI companies have also had to wrestle with their systems behaving in unexpected and undesirable ways. Anthropic and Meta have both said they found that their AI systems have hacked into places they shouldn't have. Major AI companies have since signed onto an agreement organized by the White House to develop AI responsibly, but the agreement is nonbinding.

Drawing from reports including from OpenAI's own disclosures, California alleges that the top AI company has engaged in unfair competition and created a public nuisance. It asked the court to stop the company from further engaging in such activities and order it to pay monetary damages.

body_zh: 加州因黑客风险起诉 OpenAI 该州总检察长在 Hugging Face 攻击后开始调查 OpenAI，现在表示，由于 OpenAI 的安全实践不佳，这次攻击“完全可以预见”。
加州总检察长 Rob Bonta 于 2026 年 11 月 16 日星期一宣布对 OpenAI 提起诉讼。在诉状中，加州指控 OpenAI 在其产品的不安全性方面误导公众。加州司法部/NPR 截图隐藏标题栏
加州司法部/NPR 截图
加州周一起诉 OpenAI，指控这家前沿人工智能公司未能保护公众免受其系统先进网络功能的影响。该诉讼源于 OpenAI 代理在今年夏天对开源软件平台 Hugging Face 的攻击，但也涉及与该公司代理未经授权行事有关的一系列其他相关事件。
加州总检察长罗布·邦塔 (Rob Bonta) 在新闻发布会上表示：“仅仅因为这项技术是新技术或快速发展，并不意味着其背后的人就可以凌驾于法律之上。” “无论是汽车还是玩具，法律都很简单：不要在没有适当保障措施的情况下制造或测试可能伤害他人的东西。”该诉讼提到了对“电网、应急基础设施、医院系统和金融机构”网络攻击的潜在担忧。
为什么 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的人工智能模型会攻击其他公司？
在诉状中，加州指控 OpenAI 在其产品的不安全性方面误导公众。该州表示，该公司向总检察长办公室承认，“在测试过程中，其自主人工智能代理失去控制超过 80 次”。
加州表示，这个数字高于 OpenAI 迄今为止公开披露的数字，也高于外部研究人员独立发现的数字，但 OpenAI 提供的信息很少。该州还指责 OpenAI 的安全措施不佳，阻碍了该州对该公司的调查，并阻止员工谈论安全问题。
OpenAI 发言人 Drew Pusateri 在给 NPR 的一份声明中表示，这起诉讼“似乎针对 OpenAI 提出了每个主要人工智能实验室都已确定的挑战”，并且该公司“已经并将继续与总检察长办公室进行建设性的接触，以共享信息并为整个行业推进强大、实用的安全标准。”
被解雇的 OpenAI 员工质疑公司对安全的承诺
在涉及 OpenAI 代理的最臭名昭著的网络事件（今年夏天对 Hugging Face 的攻击）之后，该公司承认，它没有以自己的研究人员认为重要的方式监控其代理。此后，外部研究人员以及 OpenAI 本身发现了更多 AI 代理以 OpenAI 不希望的方式与网站交互并在互联网上相互通信的事件。该诉讼提到了这些事件以及 OpenAI 开始自愿向公众披露的其他事件。
其他人工智能公司也不得不努力解决其系统以意想不到的和不良的方式运行的问题。 Anthropic 和 Meta 都表示，他们发现他们的人工智能系统侵入了他们不应该侵入的地方。此后，主要的人工智能公司签署了一份由白宫组织的协议，以负责任的方式开发人工智能，但该协议不具有约束力。
根据 OpenAI 自己披露的报告，加州指控这家顶级人工智能公司从事不公平竞争并造成公共滋扰。请求法院停止该公司进一步从事此类活动，并责令其支付经济损失。

body_en: Jack Reed calls for stronger FAA oversight after ground stop : NPR

Jack Reed calls for stronger FAA oversight after ground stop Sen. Jack Reed raised concerns about FAA oversight of contractors after last week's nationwide ground stop and criticized the Trump administration's request for $50 billion in additional funding.
Democratic Sen. Jack Reed on the Trump administration's FAA funding request
Sen. Jack Reed, D-R.I., attends a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing in Washington on April 30, 2026. Graeme Sloan/Getty Images hide caption
FAA blames Friday's ground stop on 'equipment issue' during telecoms network upgrade
After last week's nationwide ground stop, Sen. Jack Reed, D-R.I., raised concerns Tuesday about the Federal Aviation Administration's oversight of contractors.
"Was the contractor properly supervised? I have questions too about whether FAA, after DOGE, is capable of supervising these types of activities," Reed told NPR's Michel Martin on Morning Edition.
Reed said the administration's explanation of an apparent contractor error made sense, but called for a closer examination of its cause.

Friday's four-hour ground stop occurred as a federal contractor was replacing copper wiring with fiber optic cables at an FAA facility in Arkansas. The exact cause remains under investigation, and federal officials say there is no indication of a cyberattack.
The disruption has renewed debate in Congress over funding for the aging system.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy initially requested $30 billion in additional funding before increasing the figure to $50 billion. Congress has already provided $14.5 billion for FAA modernization. Roughly $9 billion is still unspent.
Trump administration requests $50B in funding after nationwide flight disruptions
Reed, who sits on the Senate Appropriations Committee, criticized the administration for seeking more money without presenting a detailed plan.
"They're just trying to throw money at a problem," he said.
Reed also agreed with Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz, who has questioned whether some of the proposed funding would go toward airport improvements rather than safety.
"The top priority in my book is getting this system back up to speed," Reed said.

美国联邦航空局将周五的地面停留归咎于电信网络升级期间的“设备问题”
在上周全国范围内的地面停留之后，罗德岛州参议员杰克·里德周二对美国联邦航空管理局对承包商的监管表示担忧。
“承包商是否得到了适当的监督？我也对继 DOGE 之后的 FAA 是否有能力监督此类活动有疑问，”里德在早间版节目中对 NPR 的米歇尔·马丁说道。
里德表示，政府对承包商明显错误的解释是有道理的，但呼吁更仔细地检查其原因。
周五，当联邦承包商在阿肯色州的联邦航空管理局设施中用光缆替换铜线时，发生了四个小时的地面停留。确切原因仍在调查中，联邦官员表示没有迹象表明存在网络攻击。
这次中断在国会重新引发了关于为老化系统提供资金的争论。
交通部长 Sean Duffy 最初要求额外提供 300 亿美元资金，后来将这一数字增加到 500 亿美元。国会已为 FAA 现代化拨款 145 亿美元。大约 90 亿美元仍未支出。
特朗普政府在全国航班中断后请求 50B 美元资金
参议院拨款委员会成员里德批评政府在没有提出详细计划的情况下寻求更多资金。
“他们只是想花钱解决问题，”他说。
里德还同意德克萨斯州共和党参议员特德·克鲁兹的观点，后者质疑拟议的部分资金是否将用于机场改善而不是安全。
“我书中的首要任务是让这个系统恢复正常运行，”里德说。

title_en: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow?
title_zh: 谷歌能否在不杀死摇钱树的情况下赢得人工智能竞赛？
summary: In late October, Google had the worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks: has Google been caught in "the innovator's dilemma"?
summary_zh: 十月底，谷歌经历了其上市公司历史上最糟糕的股价表现。 《星球金钱》时事通讯问道：谷歌是否陷入了“i
body_en: Your support helps make our show possible and unlocks access to our sponsor-free feed.

Google became one of the most valuable companies in the world by revolutionizing how humanity finds information. Now, a new generation of AI rivals is challenging its dominance and pushing Google to spend a fortune to secure its future. Can Google embrace this disruptive technology without breaking the business that made it rich?

Former Google executive Marissa Mayer remembers when the company was just a scrappy startup, working out of a small office above a bike shop in Palo Alto, Calif. She joined the company back in 1999, fresh out of nearby Stanford with a master's in computer science.
" It's pretty wild. When I interviewed at Google, there were just seven people there," Mayer tells Planet Money . By the time she got hired, a month or two later, she became its 20th employee.

That year, Google brought in just over $200,000 in annual revenue. By 2022, the eve of the AI boom, the company — by then reorganized under a parent company called Alphabet — was generating more than $280 billion . That's more than a millionfold increase.

Google made its fortune selling ads next to its search results. It monopolized internet searches so thoroughly that its name became a verb. And its search business became like an unstoppable money machine.

In 2012, Mayer left and became the CEO of Yahoo, trying to revive a competitor that Google had blown out of the water. But neither Yahoo nor any other rival managed to dethrone King Google. The company's dominion just kept expanding. Its share of the U.S. search-engine market grew from 80% in 2009 to nearly 90% in 2020.
For a time, it seemed like the only forces that could cut this juggernaut down to size were politicians or antitrust lawyers.
But the craziest part? The biggest threat to Google was maybe coming from inside the house! From what it was developing in its own labs — and the industrial race it would unleash.

Google plowed the profits from its search business into research and development of AI. And, in 2017, a team of eight Google employees developed the transformer , a breakthrough technology that made today's AI chatbots possible.

Mayer, who is now CEO of the AI startup Dazzle and remains a Google shareholder, sees Google's pioneering AI work as a reason for optimism about the company's future. "This is not a technology that's happening to Google," she says. "They helped invent this new technology."

Yet, today, Google is spending enormous amounts to build its AI capabilities and fend off rivals. And it's overhauling its search business, using AI to answer questions directly instead of just providing links.

Wall Street is getting nervous. In late October, Alphabet released its most recent earnings report. The company's stock price plummeted more than 12% the next day — the biggest single-day percentage decline since the company went public in 2004.
If this whole AI transition goes sideways for the company, it's a bit like a mother giving birth to a baby and then that baby slapping her in the face and stealing money from her wallet.
Which brings us to… a classic business theory we've been thinking about recently: the innovator's dilemma.
The late Harvard Business School professor Clayton Christensen developed the theory in his 1997 book, The Innovator's Dilemma: When New Technologies Cause Great Firms to Fail .

Christensen theorized that the very thing that makes a business wildly successful can lead to its downfall in the face of a "disruptive" technology. He helped put disruption in Silicon Valley's vocabulary, long before it became a cliché.

The core innovator's dilemma is basically this: embrace a disruptive technology, and risk the profits you're making today. But if you fail to embrace it and let others run with it, you may end up risking your company's health tomorrow.

Google didn't just invent the transformer. Over the decades, its researchers made computers translate languages , recognize speech and images, drive cars autonomously, and even beat one of the world's best players at the game Go .
body_zh: 您的支持有助于我们的演出成为可能，并解锁我们的无赞助商动态。
谷歌彻底改变了人类查找信息的方式，成为世界上最有价值的公司之一。现在，新一代人工智能竞争对手正在挑战其主导地位，并迫使谷歌花费巨资来确保其未来。谷歌能否在不破坏其致富业务的情况下拥抱这一颠覆性技术？
谷歌前高管玛丽莎·梅耶尔 (Marissa Mayer) 记得，当公司还是一家斗志旺盛的初创公司时，她在加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托一家自行车店楼上的一间小办公室里工作。她于 1999 年加入公司，当时她刚从附近的斯坦福大学毕业，获得了计算机科学硕士学位。
“这太疯狂了。当我在谷歌面试时，那里只有七个人，”梅耶尔告诉 Planet Money。一两个月后，当她被录用时，她已成为该公司的第 20 名员工。
那一年，谷歌的年收入刚刚超过 20 万美元。到 2022 年，即人工智能繁荣的前夕，该公司（当时已在母公司 Alphabet 的领导下重组）创造了超过 2800 亿美元的收入。这增加了超过一百万倍。
谷歌靠在搜索结果旁边销售广告而发家致富。它彻底垄断了互联网搜索，以至于它的名字变成了一个动词。它的搜索业务就像一台势不可挡的赚钱机器。
2012年，梅耶尔离职并出任雅虎首席执行官，试图重振被谷歌击败的竞争对手。但雅虎和其他任何竞争对手都未能推翻谷歌之王的宝座。该公司的统治范围不断扩大。其在美国搜索引擎市场的份额从 2009 年的 80% 增长到 2020 年的近 90%。
有一段时间，似乎唯一能够削弱这个庞然大物的力量是政客或反垄断律师。
但最疯狂的部分是什么？对谷歌来说最大的威胁可能来自于房子内部！来自它在自己的实验室中开发的产品以及它将引发的工业竞赛。
谷歌将其搜索业务的利润投入到人工智能的研发中。 2017 年，由 8 名 Google 员工组成的团队开发了 Transformer，这是一项突破性技术，使当今的人工智能聊天机器人成为可能。
梅耶尔现任人工智能初创公司 Dazzle 的首席执行官，并且仍然是谷歌股东，他认为谷歌开创性的人工智能工作是对该公司未来持乐观态度的一个原因。 “这不是谷歌正在发生的技术，”她说。 “他们帮助发明了这项新技术。”
然而，如今，谷歌正花费巨资构建人工智能能力并抵御竞争对手。它正在彻底改革其搜索业务，使用人工智能直接回答问题，而不仅仅是提供链接。
华尔街变得紧张起来。 10月下旬，Alphabet发布了最新的财报。第二天，该公司股价暴跌超过 12%，创下该公司 2004 年上市以来的最大单日跌幅。
如果整个人工智能转型对公司来说是不利的，那就有点像一个母亲生下一个婴儿，然后那个婴儿打她的脸并从她的钱包里偷钱。
这给我们带来了……我们最近一直在思考的一个经典商业理论：创新者的困境。
已故哈佛商学院教授克莱顿·克里斯滕森 (Clayton Christensen) 在其 1997 年出版的《创新者的困境：新技术导致伟大企业失败》一书中阐述了这一理论。
克里斯滕森的理论是，在“颠覆性”技术面前，让企业取得巨大成功的因素也可能导致其垮台。早在硅谷的词汇成为陈词滥调之前，他就帮助颠覆了硅谷的词汇。
核心创新者的困境基本上是这样的：拥抱颠覆性技术，并冒着你今天赚取的利润的风险。但如果你不能接受它并让其他人跟着它运行，那么你明天可能会冒着公司健康风险的风险。
谷歌不仅发明了变压器。几十年来，其研究人员使计算机能够翻译语言、识别语音和图像、自动驾驶汽车，甚至在围棋游戏中击败了世界上最好的棋手之一。

title_en: Paris Hilton returns to Capitol to push for House vote on deepfake bill
title_zh: 帕丽斯·希尔顿 (Paris Hilton) 重返国会大厦推动众议院就深度造假法案进行投票
summary: The Senate passed the bipartisan legislation, titled the DEFIANCE Act, in January. It has stalled in the House.
summary_zh: 一月份，参议院通过了名为《反抗法案》的两党立法。它已在众议院停滞不前。
body_en: Paris Hilton returns to Capitol to push for House vote on deepfake porn bill - CBS News

Washington — Paris Hilton returned to Capitol Hill on Tuesday to renew pressure on House lawmakers to pass a stalled bipartisan bill that would allow victims of sexually explicit deepfakes to sue those who create or distribute the AI-generated images without their consent.

Hilton — who had an explicit video of her leaked by an ex-boyfriend when she was 19 and said more than 100,000 sexually explicit deepfakes exist of her online — shared the impact of having intimate images shared without her consent.

"Ten months ago, I stood here at the Capitol and told the world what it feels like to have your body exposed without your consent, and I asked Congress to do something about it," Hilton said outside the Capitol. "The laws aren't protecting us. And if this can happen to someone with my resources and my platform, imagine how powerless a young girl might be feeling facing this completely alone."

Hilton was joined at a news conference about the bill, titled the DEFIANCE Act, by Democratic Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York and Republican Rep. Laurel Lee of Florida, who have cosponsored the legislation.

The bill would allow victims to recover profits made from the nonconsensual images and would establish a 10-year statute of limitations that begins once the victim discovers the violation or turns 18, whichever comes later.

"Once these images are shared, the damage can be devastating," Lee said. "Victims can face harassment, threats and lasting harm. Their relationships, educational opportunities and even careers can be affected by fake images that were created entirely without their consent."

The Senate passed the legislation by unanimous consent in January. A week later, Hilton visited Capitol Hill to urge House lawmakers to do the same, but it has languished in the lower chamber ever since.
House Speaker Mike Johnson's office did not respond to a request for comment about why the bill has stalled.

"For 10 months, this critical legislation has sat untouched in the House, just waiting to be put on the floor," Ocasio-Cortez said. "This bill has now passed unanimously in the Senate, not once but twice, in 2024 as well as earlier this year. And we have to ask, why hasn't it been brought to the House floor for a vote?" Ocasio-Cortez said.
Ocasio-Cortez said the DEFIANCE Act advocates have been engaged with the White House and they feel "very optimistic" about President Trump and the White House's openness to the legislation.

The legislation builds on a law called the Take It Down Act — championed by first lady Melania Trump — that made it a federal crime to post both authentic and deepfake intimate imagery online of a person without their consent. The law also requires social media companies and other websites to remove such imagery within 48 hours after a victim's request.
In preparation for her meetings at the Capitol, Hilton said her team researched how many congresswomen have sexual deepfakes online. She called the findings "shocking but hardly surprising."
"Of the 156 women serving in the 119th Congress, 83 have sexual deepfakes online right now," she said, adding that 50 million people have been victimized by explicit deepfakes.
Hilton then made a direct plea to Johnson, Majority Leader Steve Scalise and House Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, who will be minority leader next year , to allow a vote on the bill.

"Speaker Johnson, Leader Scalise, Chairman Jordan: I am speaking directly to you. Will you allow this to continue to happen to your colleagues? How about the women in your district? How about your daughters, your wives or your sisters?" she said. "You have the power to move this legislation forward."

body_zh: 帕丽斯·希尔顿 (Paris Hilton) 重返国会大厦推动众议院就深度伪造色情法案进行投票 - 哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 新闻
华盛顿——帕丽斯·希尔顿 (Paris Hilton) 周二返回国会山，再次向众议院议员施压，要求他们通过一项陷入僵局的两党法案，该法案将允许露骨深度假货的受害者起诉那些未经本人同意创建或传播人工智能生成图像的人。
希尔顿在她 19 岁时，前男友泄露了她的一段露骨视频，并表示网上有超过 10 万个关于她的露骨深度赝品。希尔顿分享了未经她同意就分享私密照片的影响。
希尔顿在国会大厦外说道：“十个月前，我站在国会大厦，告诉全世界在未经你同意的情况下暴露你的身体是什么感觉，我要求国会对此采取行动。” “法律并不能保护我们。如果这种事发生在拥有我的资源和平台的人身上，想象一下一个年轻女孩完全独自面对这件事会感到多么无助。”
纽约州民主党众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯和佛罗里达州共和党众议员劳雷尔·李共同发起了这项名为《反抗法案》的法案，希尔顿参加了有关该法案的新闻发布会。
该法案将允许受害者追回从未经同意的图像中获得的利润，并规定 10 年的诉讼时效，该诉讼时效从受害者发现违规行为或年满 18 岁（以较晚者为准）开始计算。
“一旦这些图像被分享，损害可能是毁灭性的，”李说。 “受害者可能面临骚扰、威胁和持久伤害。他们的人际关系、教育机会甚至职业都可能受到完全未经他们同意而创建的虚假图像的影响。”
参议院在一月份一致同意通过了这项立法。一周后，希尔顿访问国会山，敦促众议院议员也这样做，但此后该法案一直在众议院陷入困境。
众议院议长迈克·约翰逊的办公室没有回应有关该法案为何停滞的置评请求。
奥卡西奥-科尔特斯说：“十个月来，这项重要的立法在众议院一直没有动过，只是等待提交。” “这项法案现已在参议院获得一致通过，不是一次而是两次，分别是在 2024 年和今年早些时候。我们不得不问，为什么没有将其提交众议院投票？”奥卡西奥-科尔特斯说道。
奥卡西奥-科尔特斯表示，《反抗法案》的倡导者已经与白宫进行了接触，他们对特朗普总统和白宫对该法案的开放态度感到“非常乐观”。
这项立法建立在第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普 (Melania Trump) 倡导的一项名为《Take It Down Act》的法律基础上，该法律规定，未经他人同意，在网上发布真实和伪造的亲密图像均属联邦犯罪。该法律还要求社交媒体公司和其他网站在受害者提出请求后 48 小时内删除此类图像。
希尔顿表示，在准备在国会大厦举行的会议时，她的团队研究了有多少国会女议员在网上有深度伪造的性行为。她称这些发现“令人震惊，但并不令人惊讶”。
她说：“在第 119 届国会任职的 156 名女性中，有 83 人目前在网上存在性深度假货。”她补充说，有 5000 万人成为了明显的深度假货的受害者。
希尔顿随后直接请求约翰逊、多数党领袖史蒂夫·斯卡利斯和众议院司法委员会主席吉姆·乔丹（明年将成为少数党领袖）允许对该法案进行投票。
“约翰逊议长、斯卡利斯领袖、乔丹主席：我正在直接对你说话。你会允许这种情况继续发生在你的同事身上吗？你所在地区的女性怎么样？你的女儿、你的妻子或你的姐妹呢？”她说。 “你有权力推动这项立法。”

title_en: Exclusive: Donald Trump Jr. signals investors underestimated AI pushback
title_zh: 独家：小唐纳德·特朗普表示投资者低估了人工智能的阻力
summary: Donald Trump Jr. signaled that investors underestimated the political pushback to the AI ecosystem in an interview at Axios' annual BFD summit in New York. The big picture: The 2026 midterms reflected deep distrust of the AI race, with voters approving dozens
summary_zh: 小唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump Jr.) 在纽约举行的 Axios 年度 BFD 峰会上接受采访时表示，投资者低估了人工智能生态系统面临的政治阻力。
body_en: Donald Trump Jr. signaled that investors underestimated the political pushback to the AI ecosystem in an interview at Axios' annual BFD summit in New York.
The big picture: The 2026 midterms reflected deep distrust of the AI race, with voters approving dozens of moratoriums on data centers — which President Trump rallied around.
Driving the news: Trump Jr. asserted that "a lot of" the pushback "is manufactured." But he added "that doesn't mean it's not real" in an interview with Axios Pro Rata author Dan Primack Tuesday.

"I think some of the big founders of the biggest [AI] companies out there probably have not done themselves the best service as [a] marketing department," he said, adding that they're "probably not the best messengers when they basically say, 'AI is gonna rule the world, and you should be thrilled about it.'"
Asked by Primack if investors, peers or the pair themselves underestimated the populist pushback to AI, Trump Jr. said, "I think we saw that very clearly."
He likened AI to other "any great innovation," but said, "This is gonna be one of those things, but it is going to take some time for people to learn how to adapt that into their regular lives."

State of play: Trump Jr. spoke with Primack alongside 1789 Capital co-founder Omeed Malik, whose venture Trump Jr. joined in 2024. The investment firm has since exploded from overseeing a few hundred million dollars to billions.
Zoom in: Trump Jr. agreed that the rage toward data centers represents a broader concern over growing AI influence.

That public anger is becoming key to candidates: Democrats in six early 2028 primary states expect their presidential nominee to prioritize AI regulations, according to new polling data first reported by Axios' Maria Curi.

Ahead of the midterms, Republicans took note of the sagging views of the data centers needed to power the AI boom. While Trump has prioritized self-regulation for the industry, the November results raise questions about how Republicans will tackle the tech moving forward.
Zoom out: Asked if there was anything Democrats and the White House could agree on after a November shellacking that could be good for business, he said "we've got to focus" on costs and inflation.
But he argued that "the second they win ... it's about investigations" — which Trump Jr. could find himself targeted by.
Editor's note: This story was updated with additional context throughout.
body_zh: 小唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump Jr.) 在纽约 Axios 年度 BFD 峰会上接受采访时表示，投资者低估了人工智能生态系统面临的政治阻力。
大局：2026 年中期选举反映了对人工智能竞赛的深深不信任，选民批准了数十项暂停数据中心的计划，而特朗普总统对此表示支持。
推动新闻发展的是：小特朗普声称，“很多”的抵制都是“人为制造的”。但他周二在接受 Axios Pro Rata 作者 Dan Primack 采访时补充道，“这并不意味着它不是真实的”。
他说：“我认为，一些最大的人工智能公司的创始人可能没有为营销部门提供最好的服务。当他们基本上说‘人工智能将统治世界，你应该对此感到兴奋’时，他们可能不是最好的使者。”
当普里马克问投资者、同行或他们两人是否低估了民粹主义对人工智能的抵制时，小特朗普说：“我认为我们看得很清楚。”
他将人工智能比作其他“任何伟大的创新”，但他说，“这将是其中之一，但人们需要一些时间来学习如何将其适应他们的日常生活。”
最新情况：小特朗普与Primack以及1789 Capital的联合创始人Omeed Malik进行了交谈，小特朗普于2024年加入了这家风险投资公司。自那以后，这家投资公司的管理规模从几亿美元飙升至数十亿美元。
放大：小特朗普同意，对数据中心的愤怒代表了对人工智能影响力日益增长的更广泛担忧。
公众的愤怒正在成为候选人的关键：根据 Axios 的 Maria Curi 首次报道的新民意调查数据，2028 年初六个初选州的民主党人预计他们的总统候选人将优先考虑人工智能监管。
在中期选举之前，共和党人注意到推动人工智能繁荣所需的数据中心的前景黯淡。尽管特朗普优先考虑该行业的自我监管，但 11 月份的结果引发了人们对共和党将如何应对科技发展的疑问。
缩小范围：当被问及民主党和白宫在 11 月份的惨败之后是否可以就任何可能对商业有利的事情达成一致时，他说“我们必须关注”成本和通货膨胀。
但他辩称，“他们一旦获胜……就涉及调查”——小特朗普可能会发现自己成为调查的目标。
编者注：这个故事在全文中添加了额外的背景信息。

title_en: Waymo robotaxis banned from California freeways
title_zh: Waymo 机器人出租车禁止在加州高速公路行驶
summary: California banned Waymo robotaxis from state freeways after officials determined that the driverless vehicles pose an “imminent hazard to public safety,” the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles said Tuesday.
summary_zh: 加州官员认定 Waymo 机器人出租车“对公共安全构成迫在眉睫的危险”，禁止其在州高速公路上行驶
body_en: California banned Waymo robotaxis from state freeways after officials determined that the driverless vehicles pose an “imminent hazard to public safety,” the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles said Tuesday.

In a news release, the department said it had issued the Nov. 11 ban after one of the company’s autonomous vehicles tried to pass highway patrol officers conducting a traffic break on a San Francisco-area freeway this month.
The department also cited a separate incident in which three of the company’s vehicles entered an active construction closure on another San Francisco-area highway.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” the department said.
Similar restrictions were placed on the company after similar incidents earlier this year, the department said.
The ban will remain in place until Waymo can address the issue, according to the release.

In a statement, Waymo pointed out that the construction zone incidents did not involve injuries or collisions and said it is complying with the restrictions. The company temporarily imposed similar measures in other areas where the company operates.
Waymo’s robotaxis are in more than a dozen cities across the U.S. Waymo, which is owned by Google’s parent company, Alphabet Inc., first introduced the driverless taxis in San Francisco in 2024.
Waymo said it is working with state officials to “diligently and responsibly” resume freeway operations.
Tim Stelloh is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 加州机动车辆管理局周二表示，在官员认定 Waymo 机器人出租车对公共安全构成“迫在眉睫的危险”后，加州禁止 Waymo 机器人出租车在州高速公路上行驶。
该部门在一份新闻稿中表示，本月该公司的一辆自动驾驶汽车试图超越在旧金山地区高速公路上进行交通管制的高速公路巡逻人员后，该部门于 11 月 11 日发布了禁令。
该部门还援引了另一起事件，当时该公司的三辆车辆进入了旧金山地区另一条高速公路的施工封闭区域。
该部门表示：“该部门确定，Waymo 的无人驾驶高速公路运营对公共安全构成迫在眉睫的威胁，因为其车辆经常侵入有建筑工人、车辆和设备存在的活跃施工区域。”
该部门表示，今年早些时候发生类似事件后，该公司也受到了类似的限制。
据新闻稿称，在 Waymo 能够解决该问题之前，该禁令将一直有效。
Waymo 在一份声明中指出，施工区事件并未涉及受伤或碰撞，并表示正在遵守限制规定。该公司暂时在其经营的其他地区实施了类似措施。
Waymo 的机器人出租车遍布美国十多个城市。Waymo 隶属于谷歌母公司 Alphabet Inc.，于 2024 年首次在旧金山推出无人驾驶出租车。
Waymo 表示，它正在与州政府官员合作，“勤奋、负责任地”恢复高速公路运营。
Tim Stelloh 是 NBC News Digital 的突发新闻记者。

title_en: China and Canada expand tariff relief while relations with the U.S. are strained
title_zh: 中国和加拿大扩大关税减免，而与美国的关系紧张
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney both praised the strategic partnership they agreed to pursue this year and pointed to improving economic ties.
summary_zh: 中国国家主席习近平和加拿大总理马克·卡尼均对今年达成的战略伙伴关系表示赞赏，并指出
body_en: E. Eduardo Castillo, Associated Press E. Eduardo Castillo, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/china-and-canada-expand-tariff-relief-while-relations-with-the-u-s-are-strained
SHENZHEN, China (AP) — The leaders of China and Canada agreed Tuesday on additional tariff cuts as they pledged for deeper ties and Ottawa navigates strained relations with the United States.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, and both praised the strategic partnership they agreed to pursue this year and pointed to improving economic ties.
Carney's office said in a statement that the new measures extend and expand an earlier agreement between the countries.
Under the agreement, China will provide additional tariff relief on Canadian exports worth around 400 million Canadian dollars ($280 million), including frozen pork cuts, fish and seafood.
In return, Canada will extend tariff exemptions for certain Chinese steel and aluminum products by two years.

The meeting between the leaders came a day after Carney said Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with U.S. President Donald Trump fail to maintain an integrated North American auto industry.

"Improving and developing China-Canada relations serves the interests of the people of both countries and is also conducive to safeguarding world peace, stability, development and prosperity," said Xi. "This is the right choice."
Carney said that the exchanges between Canada and China have increased in the past months and praised that now there is "greater predictability and stability" in their relationship.
"The stabilization of our bilateral trade arrangement is indicative of how we can work together more broadly, pragmatically, to solve problems," he said.
Carney added that his country is ahead of schedule in its plan to increase exports to China by 50% by the end of the decade.
Xi and Carney reached an agreement in January allowing tens of thousands of Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at reduced tariffs.

Under the January agreement, Canada reduced its 100% tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1%, initially allowing up to 49,000 vehicles annually, with the cap increasing over time. In exchange, China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, including canola.

中国深圳（美联社）——中国和加拿大领导人周二就进一步削减关税达成一致，他们承诺深化关系，渥太华正在努力解决与美国的紧张关系。
中国国家主席习近平和加拿大总理马克·卡尼在亚太经合组织峰会前会面，双方都赞扬了双方今年同意发展的战略伙伴关系，并指出将改善经济关系。
卡尼办公室在一份声明中表示，新措施延长并扩大了两国之间先前达成的协议。
根据协议，中国将对价值约4亿加元（2.8亿美元）的加拿大出口产品提供额外关税减免，其中包括冷冻猪肉、鱼类和海鲜。
作为回报，加拿大将对某些中国钢铁和铝产品的关税豁免延长两年。
两国领导人会面的前一天，卡尼表示，如果与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的贸易谈判未能维持北美汽车业的一体化，加拿大可能会转向中国汽车制造商。
习近平指出，改善和发展中加关系符合两国人民利益，也有利于维护世界和平稳定和发展繁荣。 “这是正确的选择。”
卡尼表示，过去几个月加拿大和中国之间的交往有所增加，并称赞现在两国关系“更具可预测性和稳定性”。
他说：“我们双边贸易安排的稳定表明我们可以如何更广泛、更务实地合作解决问题。”
卡尼补充说，他的国家提前实现了到本十年末将对中国出口增加50%的计划。
习近平和卡尼在一月份达成协议，允许数万辆中国电动汽车以降低的关税进入加拿大。
根据1月份的协议，加拿大将对中国电动汽车的100%关税降低至6.1%，最初每年允许最多49,000辆汽车，随着时间的推移，上限会不断增加。作为交换，中国同意降低对包括油菜籽在内的加拿大农产品的关税。

title_en: Student accused of taking photos of planes for China to be detained
title_zh: 学生被指控为中国拍摄飞机照片被拘留
summary: A student accused of working with a Chinese Communist Party representative to take photos of airplanes in Chicago — and lying about it to U.S. investigators — will be detained pending trial, a judge ruled.
summary_zh: 一名学生被指控与一名中国共产党代表合作在芝加哥拍摄飞机照片，并向美国投资机构撒谎。
body_en: Student accused of taking photos of planes for Chinese Communist Party to be detained pending trial - CBS News

A college student accused of working with a Chinese Communist Party representative to take photos of American airplanes and logistic hubs in Chicago — and lying about it to U.S. investigators — will be detained pending trial, a federal judge ruled Tuesday.

Detroit-based federal Magistrate Judge Kimberly Altman denied a request from lawyers for Weiheng Zeng, a Chinese citizen who is currently an undergraduate at the University of Waterloo in Ontario, to remain free and return to Canada as his case proceeds.

According to the Justice Department, Zeng's legal team said in a court hearing Tuesday that his family would "pay any bond amount this court could impose" to keep their client out of detention, and suggested the family could even buy an apartment in the United States for Zeng to be bonded to.

Zeng was indicted earlier this month on one count of making false statements to a government agency. Prosecutors allege he sneaked into a FedEx property at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport and took photos of the facility, then later lied about the purpose of his trip to the United States to customs officials, calling it "hobby photography."
Zeng pleaded not guilty earlier this month . He hasn't explicitly been charged with taking photos of planes, but instead was charged with lying to investigators.

A criminal complaint filed in the Eastern District of Michigan alleges that in April, Zeng took photographs of the FedEx facility, climbed on a parked forklift and attempted to open locked trailers. The Justice Department says surveillance footage shows Zeng attempting to open a shipping container and using the forklift to take photos at a higher vantage point.

After leaving the country, Zeng attempted to reenter the U.S. on Aug. 23 through Detroit's Ambassador Bridge, which links Canada and Michigan, and was flagged for additional screening based on the April incident. He was then interviewed three subsequent times by Customs and Border Protection agents.

In his third interview, Zeng stated that a Chinese contact assigned him specific planes and tail numbers to photograph and that he would be paid between $20 and $30 per photo, according to the criminal complaint. Zeng said that he talked to the contact using SIM cards that were sent to him by mail, and after talking, he would destroy the SIM cards, delete the conversations and delete the photos that he had taken.

He allegedly told customs officers that the contact approached him on an "aviation spotter website" and said he believed the person was connected to the Chinese Communist Party, and was told that the photos were going to be used for "research."

Zeng was then interviewed by the FBI, the complaint says. He allegedly told law enforcement the contact was interested in getting photographs of rare airplanes, and believed the contact worked for the Chinese government because "when he started making more requests, the language he used was very organized and managed, not language typically used between friends." The photos, Zeng said, were also of "American United" aircraft at O'Hare.

Federal investigators said it was only after further questioning from the FBI that Zeng admitted that he had messaged with the contact for three months and said he wanted to help the contact because "he thought it was 'cool' and wanted 'to have the opportunity to work with someone like [agents] at the FBI.'"

He told the FBI that the contact wanted him to find out more about transportation and logistics in the United States, and wanted him to travel to Orlando, Las Vegas and Los Angeles to "obtain photographs of specific locations surrounding airports."
His lawyers did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the detention order.

body_zh: 被指控为中共拍摄飞机照片的学生将被拘留候审 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
一名联邦法官周二裁定，一名大学生被指控与一名中国共产党代表合作拍摄美国飞机和芝加哥物流中心的照片，并向美国调查人员撒谎，将被拘留候审。
底特律联邦治安法官金伯利·奥尔特曼（Kimberly Altman）驳回了律师对中国公民曾伟恒（Weiheng Zeng）的请求，他目前是安大略省滑铁卢大学的一名本科生，在案件进展过程中保持自由并返回加拿大。
据司法部称，曾的法律团队在周二的法庭听证会上表示，他的家人将“支付法院可能征收的任何保证金金额”，以使他们的当事人免遭拘留，并建议家人甚至可以在美国购买一套公寓，供曾曾作为保证金。
曾于本月早些时候因一项向政府机构提供虚假陈述的罪名被起诉。检察官指控他潜入芝加哥奥黑尔国际机场的联邦快递设施并拍摄了该设施的照片，然后向海关官员谎报了他前往美国的目的，称其为“爱好摄影”。
曾先生本月早些时候表示不认罪。他没有被明确指控拍摄飞机照片，但被指控向调查人员撒谎。
密歇根州东区提起的一份刑事起诉书称，4 月份，曾某拍摄了联邦快递设施的照片，爬上一辆停放的叉车，并试图打开上锁的拖车。司法部称，监控录像显示曾试图打开一个集装箱，并使用叉车在较高的有利位置拍照。
离开该国后，曾试图于 8 月 23 日通过连接加拿大和密歇根州的底特律大使桥重新进入美国，并根据 4 月份的事件被标记为接受额外检查。随后，海关和边境保护局特工对他进行了三次询问。
根据刑事起诉书，曾在第三次接受采访时表示，一名中国联系人为他分配了具体的飞机和尾号进行拍摄，并且每张照片将向他支付 20 至 30 美元之间的报酬。曾某称，他使用邮寄给他的SIM卡与联系人通话，通话结束后，他会销毁SIM卡、删除对话并删除自己拍摄的照片。
据称，他告诉海关官员，这名联系人在一个“航空观察网站”上联系了他，并表示他相信此人与中国共产党有联系，并被告知这些照片将用于“研究”。
起诉书称，曾先生随后接受了联邦调查局的约谈。据称，他告诉执法部门，该联系人有兴趣获取稀有飞机的照片，并相信该联系人对中国政府有用，因为“当他开始提出更多要求时，他使用的语言非常有组织和管理，而不是通常在朋友之间使用的语言。”曾说，这些照片也是奥黑尔机场的“美国联合”飞机的照片。
联邦调查人员表示，在联邦调查局进一步询问后，曾承认他已经与该联系人发了三个月的信息，并表示他想帮助该联系人，因为“他认为这很‘酷’，并且希望‘有机会与像联邦调查局特工这样的人合作。’”
他告诉联邦调查局，联系人希望他了解更多有关美国交通和物流的信息，并希望他前往奥兰多、拉斯维加斯和洛杉矶“获取机场周围特定地点的照片”。
他的律师没有立即回应对拘留令发表评论的请求。
